Some sort of large prybar of a make and manufacturer you've never seen before.  On the heavier end is a set of thick, crabclaw like shears connected to a hydraulic piston, capable of cutting or prying through metal with great force.  The Exodii use these for general purpose breaching and scrapping heavy machines, and it's been retrofitted to run on their bionic power.

A metal pole saw covered in faded orange paint and warning labels written in an unknown language.  The circular blade at the end is over an inch thick, its deeply dished grooves suggesting its purpose as a digging implement rather than a cutter.  The Exodii use these to chew through reinforced walls like concrete or solid steel, and it's been retrofitted to run on their bionic power.
data.//0: This should have some unique faults that circular saws and other saws should also have too.

data.description: Short, sharp claws made from a high-tech metal.
A foot-long blade made from high-tech alloy and edged with bonded nanocrystals.

A long strip of braided leather with a handle on one end.  Originally developed to settle disagreements with cattle, it's better used now for flaying the rotten flesh off of walking corpses.  Great for when a problem comes along.

The "cat 'o nine tails", a handle with nine short leather whips, each sporting a razor-sharp metal tip.  This ancient instrument of torture causes massive bleeding, but by design is inefficient as a weapon.
data.//: There's no way you can swing this thing without hitting SOMETHING.

data.description: A high-powered stun gun.  Use this item to attempt to electrocute an adjacent enemy, temporarily paralyzing them.
data.//: Yes, this is smaller than its magazine well. Go with it.

data.description: An agricultural tool with a long wooden shaft and four spikes.  Normally used to lift hay.
A simple wooden pole with one end sharpened to a point.
A stout pole with one end sharpened to a point.
A stout wooden pole with a fire-hardened point.
A stout wooden pole with a whittled point.
You've gone through the effort of making a proper spear shaft, but instead of attaching something sharp to the end you just whittled a point into the wood.  The peak of pointy stick technology.
This farming tool has been modified into an improvised weapon by rotating its blade 90 degrees, transforming it into a deadly giant blade on the end of a stick.  It's quite fragile, however.

data.//: Name changed to simple makeshift glaive, but changing the id would break e.g.  tilesets.
data.description: A large blade attached to a stout section of tree branch.  It could do a considerable amount of damage, but the blade isn't secured very well and could easily break off.
A stout tree branch that has been carefully split and reinforced.  At the split point, a sharp blade has been bolted into place and reinforced with layers of sturdy wrapped bindings.
A flimsy pole made of wood with a basic metal spike tied to it.  It's barely sharp, and crudely constructed, but it will keep the zombies out of arm's reach until you can find something better.

A flimsy pole made of wood with a knife bound to the end.  It's long enough to slice from a distance, but the knife isn't that well attached.  You could take a bit more time to carefully split the shaft and attach the knife blade more permanently.
A long stick that has been carefully split and reinforced.  At the split point, a sharp blade has been bolted into place and reinforced with layers of sturdy wrapped bindings.
A stout wooden pole with the blade of a knife bolted into place at the end.  The shape of a knife blade isn't ideal for a spear, but it's still very sharp and effective.
A short do-it-yourself spear made out of a long stick with a metal spike seated and bound into place at its tip.
A stout wooden pole with a misshapen metal spike seated into the end and bolted into place.
A stout wooden pole, slightly thicker at the end, with a metal cap and a spike protruding straight up from the top.
A stout wooden pole with a spearhead worked from copper.
A stout wooden pole with a hand-forged medium steel spearhead.
A stout wooden pole with a mild steel spearhead.  Although made of low quality steel, it is still reasonably effective, if not very durable.
A stout wooden pole with a hand-forged high steel spearhead.  The high steel offers superior sharpness and penetrating power.
A stout wooden pole tipped with a hand-forged hardened steel spearhead.  The case-hardened and carefully slack quenched tip offers superior killing power, making this a spear fit for a medieval lord.

A stout wooden pole tipped with a hand-forged tempered steel spearhead.  Masterfully tempered and quenched, the bluish steel coalesces in a needle-fine point.  The shaft has been lined with a spiraling leather riser, improving control during deadly thrusts.  The king of all weapons.
A pipe with one end cut off at an angle.
Three pipes tightly fit together with one end cut down to a point.
Three pipes tightly fit together with some wrappings for a handle around one end and a sharp tip on the other.
Five pipes threaded together to form a very crude pike.  Heavy, slow, and all around cumbersome to carry and fight with.
Five pipes welded together to form a very crude pike.  Heavy, slow, and all around cumbersome to carry and fight with.
A rod of rebar that's been crudely hammered into a point.
A rod of rebar that's been cut and sharpened to a point.
Two rods of rebar welded together with a pointed tip.

An ancient Chinese spear, typically with a tassel just below the spearhead and larger than most European spears.  One of the four major weapons in folklore, alongside the dao saber, jian sword, and gun staff.
A versatile polearm with an axe blade, a spike, and other fun things attached to a long, sturdy stick.
A dull, cheaply made replica of a polearm with an axe blade, a spike, and other fun things attached to a thick pole.
A homemade halberd, made by attaching an axe head to a spear shaft.  Not as good as the real thing, but a whole heck of a lot cheaper and easier.
data.//: Average weight of wood axe head (2.5lb) and fireaxe head (6lb) + 1kg spear shaft

data.description: A nasty set of hooks and spikes set upon a shaft, with a metal endcap.  This ain't no gardening tool, and it'll hook someone very easily.
A sturdy polearm with a sizable single-edged blade on the end.
A sturdy polearm with a curved blade, made in the same manner as the katana and other Japanese blades.  Occasionally used by samurai in early periods, or by their wives in defense of the household.
A sturdy polearm with a curved blade, made in the same manner as the katana and other Japanese blades.  This one has a bit of wiggle to its blade and feels a bit shoddily made.
A dull, slightly floppy replica of a Japanese polearm with a curved blade.  With a little difficulty, you could use it administer a solid slap from a distance.
This crude facsimile of a naginata was made by attaching a machete to the end of a spear.
This crude facsimile of a naginata was made by attaching a machete to the end of a spear.  This one uses a tempered machete, making it a bit more sharp and durable.
A fire-hardened wooden spear honed to a sharper point.
An iron-tipped wooden throwing spear.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft with a fire-hardened point.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with a copper spearhead.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with a bronze spearhead.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with a steel spearhead.
A very long wooden shaft with a mild steel pike head.  Although made of low quality steel, it remains a formidable reach weapon, if somewhat less durable.
A very long wooden shaft with a hand-forged high steel pike head.  The improved steel offers better sharpness and penetration.
A very long wooden shaft tipped with a case-hardened steel pike head.  Its refined edge and hardened tip make it deadly in combat.
A very long wooden shaft tipped with a masterfully tempered steel pike head.  The blade is razor-sharp and perfectly tapered.  The pinnacle of polearm craftsmanship.
A dull, cheaply made replica of a medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with an iron spearhead.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with an iron spearhead.  The head seems to be pretty dull, and the whole thing feels poorly made.
A pole weapon with a curving single-edged blade.  Its blade bears some superficial resemblance to that of an agricultural scythe from which it likely evolved.
A well-made spear with a bronze head, Greek in origin.  Despite its large size, it was frequently used one-handed.

data.//: An other-earth interpretation of a hewing short spear, combining the hooking head of the Italian partisan spear with the short Zulu ixwa.  On par or worse than other qt_steel weapons, and uncraftable, being alien.

data.description: A steel shortspear from an alien world, made of a single, continuous piece of tempered steel.  The head is a broad cutting-stabbing implement with small hooks on either side.
A forged spear with a bronze head.
A polearm with an axe head, a small hammer on the back, and a short dagger-like spike on top.  It's less heavy than most polearms and has a smaller head, making it slightly quicker.

data.description: A bronze polearm that originated in the Shang dynasty of China, if not earlier.  It combines a spear head with the perpendicular blade of the earlier ge or dagger-axe.
A stout wooden pole with a sharp stone spearhead.
A long stick with a sharp stone spearhead.

A modern bayonet in use with the US Marine Corps, adopted in an effort to improve USMC hand-to-hand fighting capabilities.  The bayonet is optimized to function as a fighting knife, sporting an ergonomic handle that will minimize hand fatigue during combat.  The blade tip is sharper in profile than other bayonets to assist in penetrating body armor, and also features a small serrated section to provide for some utility.
data.//: Modelled after the OKC3S bayonet.

data.description: The current issue Army bayonet, before the Cataclysm anyways.  It is thick, heavy, and surprisingly sharp.  This bayonet also functions as a wire cutter, and a mediocre saw for cutting through aircraft fuselage.  That the handle and tang can be completely disassembled from the blade is surely a fact of great comfort to the soldier, survivalist, and you.

A weapon used for fencing, the most noble of all sports.  Unfortunately, a fencing foil is rather useless as a weapon due to its flexible shaft and dull tip.

What was once a mostly-harmless fencing foil has had its electrical plunger assembly removed and has been crudely sharpened to a point.  Though it still lacks a cutting edge, it is now somewhat more lethal, yet still familiar to the practiced fencer.

While this hefty-looking implement looks like a halligan prybar, it appears as if it it were grown rather than fabricated.  It's color is that of metal and natural stone, but it's surprisingly light in the hand, and bares the striations of old, dense wood.
Parts of this utility light have a curved appearance, as though the metal were grown in a lab.  Its single, round bulb will emit light if connected to power.

A huge, pot-bellied device that resembles something between a coal-burning stove and a boiler, with a wide, hinged cage covering the combustion chamber.  Three unmarked gauges sit like alien eyes upon its face.  A side-mounted crank is its only visible control.  In defiance of its apparent function, it has no exhaust vent; in its place is a hose twisted on itself several times, coiled in copper, and terminating in a bulbous back-mounted battery pack.

A thin sheet of otherworldly material etched with crude pictographs.  Upon closer inspection, the pictographs are slowly moving - animated grooves carved into the strange metal.  They show a squat, round vessel with its front opening like a jaw as a faceless humanoid places various objects, including a leaf, a wrench, and a dead animal, inside it.  Above it, three circular eyes sit empty, then begin to radiate jagged lines as a side crank is turned.  The contents of the chamber are reduced to a scribbled, lightning-bolt haze.  In the final image, the humanoid figure stands smaller than before, as the three darkened eyes focus into pupils, chasing the figure's descent.

data.description: A palm-sized shard of alien glass, reflecting light in holographic prisms.  You think you can see something in its depths.  Activate it to look closer.

effect.u_message: You glance into the depths of the shard and there is a strange sensation, as if you were experiencing someone's memories, forcing their way into your mind.  They are too foreign for you to comprehend, and they quickly pass from your own memory.  But, you realize you now possess a Passcode.  You fail for a moment to reconcile this understanding, because it's no password as you previously understood it.  It is, in fact, the sound of KÁ!

Welcome to your Emergency Survival Shelter.  We hope your stay here will be short and comfortable.  Provided are an emergency blanket, high-visibility jacket, gas mask, and food and water rations for one day, as well as an emergency lighter and flashlight.  There are further supplies in the communal cabinets should the facility be over its intended capacity.  These resources are checked and updated by FEMA on a regular basis, but if you find some items missing, please contact a FEMA supervisor at your earliest convenience.

Please wait in the shelter until an official evacuation transport arrives to take you to your homes or, in the event of a major disaster, to the nearest evacuation gathering point.

In the event that you have been evacuated under violent circumstances, FEMA recommends taking cover in the shelter's basement until help arrives.  Remember: if you leave the shelter, we cannot find you to take you to safety.

data.description: A plastic test-tube housing a fluorescent purple string of unknown material.  The string gently flickers and twitches on its own.

A transparent cube within a cube.  It seems to be made of clear plastic or glass, but it feels quite solid, despite also seeming weightless.  Impossibly, the inside seems larger than the outside - as you tilt it here and there, you can peer into its depths.  It's full of stars.
A desolate scene depicts a sea of fog broken by great mountains and jagged ruins.  The painting seems to shift ever so slightly, as if the winds depicted within were real.
A golden circlet adorned with filigree leaves and pearls.  The remnants of a white silk veil remain attached to the crown.

A serene visage carved from a large piece of ivory.  Its internal surface is completely smooth, and adorned with a a series of concentric bronze rings and grooves.  You could wear it over your face, but it lacks any way to see or comfortably breathe through it.

This medallion is engraved with the image of a fanciful beast set before a starfield.  Its head is strangely piscine, with a wide, toothy maw and no eyes.

Three articulate discs are mounted within this medallion and can be rotated independently, creating a strange, shifting pattern of holes.  You believe it to be a starchart of some kind, but the allowed movements of the discs don't seem to correspond to how stars move in the sky.

A series of tanks and tubes with ports for fluids, electricity, and input and output, this complex arrangement is made to house a brain and spine, and the most difficult to replace organs for keeping them alive.

The wiring and general shape suggest to you that this is a computer, or at least some sort of electronic device, but what it is and what role it serves is lost on you.  It's heavy and sturdy in construction.
This device looks electronic, but is unfamiliar.  It is a series of tightly fitted coppery-looking rings, set concentrically.  Wires run from each ring to an axis in the middle.

The wiring and general shape suggest to you that this is a tiny computer, or at least some sort of electronic device, but what it is and what role it serves is lost on you.  It's small enough to fit into your palm.
This device looks electronic, but is unfamiliar.  It is a series of tightly fitted coppery-looking nuts, set concentrically.  Wires run from each nut to an axis in the middle.

From the large glassy eye - the size of a small dinner plate - in the front, you deduce this is some sort of camera.  None of the inner workings make any sense to you nor resemble any camera you've seen before.

You assume from the coils of coppery wire and the protruding piston that this is some sort of motor or generator, but the design doesn't look similar to anything you've seen before, and you can't figure out how to get it to work.
This hefty parabolic dish is engraved with an unrecognizable pattern of symbols that might, at a guess, be some sort of circuitry pattern - or maybe a religious incantation.

Perfectly smooth, cool to the touch, and a dull blue-gray color, this looks almost like a perfect riverstone at first glance.  Its artificial nature is betrayed upon closer inspection by a network of intricate patterns visible as a slight difference in the reflection of light off its surface.
A block of pure aluminum at least as big as a dishwasher.
A single enormous brick of plastic, big enough for you to curl up inside if it were hollow.
A monolithic block of low carbon steel.
An enormous ingot of pure tin.
A massive solid piece of copper, covered by a blue-green patina.
An absolutely massive block of pure zinc.  Bet you didn't expect that - nobody expects zinc.
A block of lead so huge you don't even want to think about how heavy it is.

A collection of hand-soldered wires leading to plugs and what looks like an exotic micro controller.  The plugs look like they could be attached to you, assuming you have an SNI (Standard Neurobionic Interface).
A collection of mismatched pipes, wires, and a central device that looks like an exotic micro controller.  Almost looks like it could be used for some form of central cooling.
Thin metallic strips with an ochre sheen, interlaid together into a flexible mesh.  You can't tell whether it's a circuit, a heat dissipation component, or a mechanical actuator.
A slightly curved plate of white metal.  It readily collects low amounts of static charge.
A collection of tiny metal strips, spheres, and other geometric primitives taken from a disassembled alien machine.
A very heavy sphere, presumably made almost entirely of gold.  The complex pattern etched across its surface implies that it might serve some exotic function.
A robotic assembly of unknown function.  Entirely made from tight-fitting metal plates, it somewhat resembles the interior of a mechanical clock.
A carved sphere embedded with small black glass screens.  It's probably a sensor of some kind.
A flexible and sharp elongated rod that gets thinner on one end, weak and clearly underdeveloped.  It has been harvested from a dead alien creature.
A small chunk of alien armor, made of material that resembles bone.  Once being a part of a bigger structure, now crumbling in your hands.

A big piece of alien armor plating, made of bone-like material.  The outer part is perforated with countless holes, reminiscent of some sort of twisted coral.  It has barbed hooks growing on the inner side.
A small statuette of some kind of fantastical creature is carved out of a rough, unnatural material.  It seems remarkably well made.

You know it as a mesmerizing black gem with beautifully etched surfaces, despite only being able to see a pure void in its place when looked at.  You cannot gauge its weight or even feel it in your hands, but it's yours now.

A very small rectangular strip of metal, presumably made of gold.  One side is etched with some barely noticeable but incredibly detailed artwork of something you don't recognize, possibly a diagram of sorts.  Sometimes you feel it resonating gently.
An extremely heavy cube with rounded edges, made of a very dense metal.  It has a swing-open door that hides neatly packaged electronics of some unknown design.
The dismantled stovetop of an electric oven.  Some electric components are still attached, but the heating elements have been pulled off.
A large, hefty steel box that was once the main body of an electric oven.  Most of the parts have been stripped.  It could be further disassembled into base materials.
The control panel and LCD from a dismantled electric oven.
The removed glass and steel door of an electric oven.
A simple sheet metal drawer that goes in the bottom of an electric oven.

data.description: Primitive yarn made from coarse plant fibers like straw or grass.  Too thick to sew with, but could be woven into a crude sheet of fabric.
A handful of oddly-shaped smallish bits of cotton, waste material from tailoring projects.  Not useful for much and usually disposed of, but they can be recycled into some thread if you really want.
A handful of oddly-shaped smallish bits of faux fur, waste material from tailoring projects.  Not useful for much and usually disposed of.

A handful of oddly-shaped smallish bits of felt, waste material from tailoring projects.  Not useful for much and usually disposed of, but they can be recycled into some wool fiber if you really want.
A handful of oddly-shaped smallish bits of fur, waste material from tailoring projects.  Not useful for much and usually disposed of.

A handful of oddly-shaped smallish bits of Kevlar fabric, waste material from tailoring projects.  Normally it would be disposed of, but since Kevlar is very difficult to make in a post-apocalyptic world, it might be worth recycling it for Kevlar thread.
A handful of oddly-shaped smallish bits of leather, waste material from tailoring projects.  Not useful for much and usually disposed of.

A misshapen section of loose carpet.  Not useful for much on its own and can be discarded.
A natural cluster of wool fibers.  Could be processed into felt patches or yarn.
A small bolt of fur from an animal, roughly six inches square.  Can be made into patchwork fur sheets or used to repair fur fabric.
A small bolt of garishly-colored faux fur, roughly six inches square.  Can be made into patchwork faux fur sheets or used to repair faux fur fabric.

A small, six-inch square patch of felt.
A six-inch square patch of Nomex fire-resistant fabric.
A rolled-up animal hide which has been scraped of extraneous hair and flesh and treated to prevent decay.  It still requires tanning to become usable leather.
A folded 12-inch by 24-inch sheet of leather made from carefully tanned animal hide.  Can be cut up or used as is.
A 12-inch by 24-inch sheet of leather.  Can be cut up or used as is.
A folded 12-inch by 24-inch sheet of leather sewn together from patches.  Can be cut up or used as is.
A rolled-up animal hide which has been scraped of extraneous hair and flesh and treated to prevent decay.  It still requires tanning to become usable fur.

A 12-inch by 24-inch sheet of fur sewn together from patches.  Can be cut up or used as is.

data.description: A 12-inch by 24-inch sheet of loose-woven Kevlar synthetic fabric, suitable for making durable cut and stab resistant clothing.  While protective, this kind of Kevlar is not suitable for making ballistic gear due to the difference in weave tightness.

data.description: A 12-inch by 24-inch sheet of fabric sewn together from Kevlar patches, suitable for making durable cut and stab resistant clothing.  This would be out of the question for ballistic Kevlar but the simpler, looser weave of this variety means it is fine to use if you lack proper material sheets.
data.//: values taken from Duponts chemical reference. 144 GSM

data.description: A small, 16-layer thick ballistic Kevlar panel.  This kind of Kevlar is precision-made by machine and features an extremely tight weave which cannot be replicated by hand.  Due to this, any damage incurred to your ballistic armor will necessitate complete replacement with a new panel.  It is not as effective as loose-woven Kevlar at stopping stab wounds, but it has no equal against the threat posed by firearms.
data.//: 12 inch by 24 inch sheets, 16 layers thick. Values actually nearly identically matched panels available for purchase.

data.description: A compressed panel of Kevlar treated with epoxy or other adhesive.  It could be used to repair items made of rigid Kevlar, and makes a decent substitute for damaged carbon fiber and the like even if it isn't exactly the same.
data.//: same as above but adding superglue. IRL this is how they are made, though using 2 part resin instead.

data.description: A large log of wood, cut from a tree.  (a)ctivate a wood axe or wood saw to cut it into planks.
A splintered piece of wood, could be used as a skewer or for kindling.
A respectable length of wood, just big enough to wrap your hand around.  Makes a decent melee weapon.
A straight section of wood, about eight feet long and a couple of inches in diameter.  Makes a decent melee weapon, and can be broken into shorter pieces for crafting.
A freshly cut bamboo stalk.  It is useful for making poles and other simple wooden items, but should be dried before use as a stick.
A dried bamboo stalk.  It can be used anywhere a bamboo-compatible stick requirement is specified and can be split into two sticks.
A stout, ten-foot pole.  Could be used similarly to a spear.  It's currently soaked with oil and quite slippery.  Once the oil penetrates the wood it can be wiped down and used for further projects.
data.//: a long pole is a single piece of wood, and the heavy stick just isn't large enough.

use_action.msg: You wipe down the long pole.
use_action.not_ready_msg: The long pole is still soaking.

data.description: A stout, ten-foot pole.  Could be used similarly to a spear.  The Cataclysm gives fresh meaning to walking softly and carrying a big stick.
data.//: a long pole is a single piece of wood, and the heavy stick just isn't large enough.

data.description: A long stick carved and sanded into a smooth staff with a slight taper, for use in making spears.  It's currently soaked with oil and quite slippery.  Once the oil penetrates the wood it can be wiped down and used for further projects.

use_action.msg: You wipe down the spear shaft.
use_action.not_ready_msg: The spear shaft is still soaking.
use_action.//: 4 hours

data.description: A long stick, sanded and treated with oil for integrity and carved into a smooth staff with a slight taper, for use in making spears.  It can also be used as a makeshift quarterstaff as-is, but is too thin to be very effective for just hitting people.
A flat, thick plank of wood, like a 2 by 4 or similar piece of dimensional lumber.  Makes a decent melee weapon if you're desperate, and can be used for all kinds of construction projects.
A part of a log rough-chopped into firewood, burned for heat for longer than recorded history.
A block of tonally appropriate wood that has been air dried for a year in preparation for being turned into a musical instrument.
Tuning pegs go on stringed instruments to both provide an anchor for the strings and to control the tightness of the wire which in turn controls the tune of the notes produced.
A short 2 by 4 plank of wood.  While less common and smaller than its 4 foot cousin it can still be very useful in carpentry.
A long 2 by 4 plank of wood.  While not as common as the 4 foot variant, still makes a decent melee weapon, and can be used for all kinds construction.
An enormous beam of solid wood, very heavy and hard to lug around, but also very sturdy for construction.  You could saw or chop it into smaller pieces, like planks or panels.
A wooden post with a 4 by 4 square base.  Posts with a length similar to this are commonly used in mailboxes or as table legs.
A wooden post with a 4 by 4 square base.  Posts with a length similar to this are commonly used as chair legs.
A wooden post with a 4 by 4 square base.  Posts with a length similar to this are commonly used in the construction of walls and floors.
A small 2x2x5 inches block of wood, primarily used for carving out small wooden objects.

A wide, thin wooden board - plywood, OSB, MDF, tongue-in-groove boards, or similar, already cut to shape.  Good for all kinds of construction, but for really big projects you'd need a proper sheet of uncut plywood or the like.
data.//: Weight and volume assumes 16 square feet of 1/2 inch plywood.  The actual size of the panel likely varies wildly and the item entry may represent several smaller pieces.

data.description: A standard 4 by 8 sheet of flat wood - usually plywood, OSB, or MDF.  Heavy and bulky, it is extremely useful for all manner of construction, but you might have to cut it to size before doing smaller projects.
data.//: Weight and volume assumes 32 square feet of 1/2 inch plywood.  Due to its enormously bulky shape, volume is higher than actual displacement volume

data.description: A giant screw carved out of solid wood, a simple component used to convert rotational energy into a downward movement of greater force.

A module that uses a combination of vector integration and egocentric mapping to find the best path available.
A module that allows for the storage and recovery of information.
A wide range of sensors meant to give the ability to perceive the surrounding world.
An array of sensors and diagnostic modules allowing a robot to perceive itself.
A module that is responsible for decision-making, it basically runs the AI of a robot.

An advanced AI core with impressive cognitive abilities.
A system that can operate most conventional weapons.

A set of rotors able to lift a small drone.
A set of human-like legs.
A set of human-like arms.

What's left when you remove all moving parts and electronics.  It's the skeleton of a turret.
What's left when you remove all moving parts and electronics.  It's the skeleton and armor of a police bot.
A set of big pointy legs, like the ones found under a tripod.
What's left when you strip an android body from its components.

Huge archives of numerous IC circuit datasheets from several major manufacturers.  Probably valuable to the right person, as it would be hard to salvage and reuse these components without them.

data.description: A 3-foot (or about 1 m) jumper cable: a short multi-stranded copper cable with power leads on either end.  Attach one end to one vehicle and the other to another, and you can transfer electrical power between the two.  Can also link power grids.

A long, thick, heavy-duty jumper cable with power leads on either end.  Attach one end to one vehicle and the other to another, and you can transfer electrical power between the two, though you expect the power loss would be noticeable.  Can also link power grids.
A long 30-foot (or about 10 m) orange extension cord for extending cables or connecting appliances.  Could be used on any appliance or other household electrical system.
An extra-long 100-foot (or about 30 m) orange extension cord for extending cables or connecting outdoor appliances.  Could be used on any appliance or other household electrical system.
An extremely heavy-duty 30-foot (or about 9 m) tow cable made from thick steel wire coated in plastic.  If attached to a vehicle, it could be used to pull another vehicle of any weight.

data.description: A crude clay pot used for cooking.
A clay teapot.  Now all you need is tea and water.
A heating element with a pot and a frame for holding coffee or other powders.  You can use it to make coffee, or other drinks if you so choose.
An electric food dehydrator, invaluable in preserving food.  Can be connected to the electric grid using cord.
This jar contains a batch of eggs in a pickling solution.  You can seal up the jar once the process is completed.
A lightweight, folding stove designed to use small hexamine tablets for cooking.  Also known as an Esbit stove.
A sealed jar holding sanitized yeast wort.  You may harvest the yeast inside when it's done culturing.
A kitchen appliance capable of slicing, chopping, shredding, grinding, pureeing, and mixing.
A simple heater powered by gasoline.  It is designed for cooking food.
A chemical heat pack, used to treat sports injuries and heat food.  It is usable only once.
A chemical heat pack, used to treat sports injuries and heat food.  This one has been used up and is chemically inert, rendering it useless.
A small heating element on a stand, powered by your electric grid.  It is indispensable for cooking and chemistry.  Try not to burn yourself.
A high end hotplate that utilizes magnetic induction coils to heat ferrous cookware directly.  It is far more efficient than a standard hotplate.
data.//: technically this should only work with iron/steel ferromagnetic cookware, as most copper/aluminum and ceramic stuff wouldn't work.  No way to do that easily though.

data.description: A homemade heat sealer unit with an air pump.  It's used for vacuum packing food to preserve it.
A self-contained camping mess kit, containing everything you might need for wilderness cooking.

data.description: This jar contains raw milk separated into cream.  It is sealed until you are ready to use it.
This jar contains raw milk separating into cream.  It transforms into a milk cream jar after 6 hours.
A simple combination of a small grindstone and a bowl-shaped stone.  Used for grinding grain, but time-consuming compared to more complex methods.

A professional-grade multi-cooker, with a short electric cord.  Its multitude of settings and features promise to handle any sort of cooking, from parboiling potatoes to cooking curry to popping popcorn.  There's no manual, but you're sure you can work it out.
A professional-grade multi-cooker, with a battery slot for camping trips or tailgating.  There is a dish cooking inside it.
A simple heater powered by kerosene.  It is designed for cooking food.
A hand-cranked press for creating vegetable oil.  A hotplate heats the raw material to increase extraction efficiency.
A barrel with a large screw press for creating vegetable oil.  A kerosene cooker heats the raw material to increase extraction efficiency.
A pasta extruder powered by a hand crank.  Useful in making pasta.  It comes with various heads to make various kinds of pasta.
This jar contains a batch of pickles set to ferment.  You can seal up the jar once the process is completed.

data.//: Should be 20 but currently recipes do not utilize this value

A simple hand-powered stone quern with a wooden handle, for grinding grain.
This jar contains a batch of sauerkraut set to ferment.  You can seal up the jar once the process is completed.
A snow machine, which freezes water and shreds it into "snow", designed to be used from the comfort of your own home!  Useful for making snow cones.

data.description: A primitive sieve constructed from woven strips of plant material.  Early sieves like this were used to sift grain, though the openings on this one are too small for that.

This is no mere strainer for noodles; it's a laboratory-grade sieve used to separate particles of certain sizes.  You could use this to do a really good job sifting flour, remove dust and soil from grain, or perhaps conduct gradation tests for any civil engineers you might know.  This one has been constructed from steel mesh.
Some fine steel mesh attached to a length of thicker steel wire, forming a rigid frame.  Useful for sieving.
A large still, useful for creating distillations of alcohol and other, more curious substances.  Features a slot for a thermometer.
A small metal teapot.  Teatime wouldn't be complete without one.
A portable heat sealer unit with an air pump.  It's used for vacuum packing food to preserve it.
A waffle iron, generally used for making waffles.

description.str: Allows you to pick a dimension to teleport to.  Travellers are adviced to use Debug Phase Movement.  To teleport back to main dimension, just leave both empty.
Reports current weather.
Start before performing some action.  Activate again to see the amount of in-game time that passed.

message.str: <context_val:ret> seconds has passed since activation of a timer.  The timer has been reset.

data.description: A large metal stand used to contain a fire.  Fires set in a brazier will not spread to surrounding flammable objects.
data.//1: Calculated as a cylinder of 21.46in diameter (numbers from Amazon listing) and 5in height - the reason for such height is the brazier is 10.4in height with the legs set out, though with hypothetically legs pulled close to the base the height would be ~50% lower hence 5in.
data.//2: Based on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BQ6JNS2H

data.description: A portable brazier fashioned from a steel bucket by punching small holes on the sides to improve the air supply.  It is too small to fit any fuel item larger than some splintered wood.  Fires set in this bucket will not spread to surrounding flammable objects.
A small, improvised wood stove, made from a metal can or similar container of the right size.  It's too small to fit anything much larger than splintered wood.  Activate it to deploy.
A foldable wood stove to safely lit fires while camping in the wilderness.  Activate it to deploy.
A large metal barrel used to contain a fire.  It has multiple holes punched in its walls for air supply.  Fires set in a fire barrel will not spread to surrounding flammable objects.
data.//: values based on real world 55 gallon metal barrel

data.description: A large metal barrel used to contain a fire.  It has multiple holes punched in its walls for air supply.  Fires set in a fire barrel will not spread to surrounding flammable objects.
data.//: values based on real world 30 gal metal barrel

data.description: A folded chair for camping.  Activate it to set it down for a place to sit.
data.//: values based on basic real world folding camp chair

data.description: Folded deck chair, deploy to sit down.
Folded plastic chair on a metal frame, deploy to sit down.
A directional antenna and accompanying tripod, folded into a shape vaguely resembling an umbrella.
A military-style folding cot.  While it may not be quite as comfortable as a bed, it's better than slumming it on the ground.

use_action.done_message: You unfold the cot and place it on the ground.

data.description: A metal butchering rack designed to hang a carcass in the air.  It is folded for easy transportation.
A metal rack designed to smoke food for better preservation and taste.  It is folded for easy transportation.  As a deployable item, it's smaller than a stationary version.
A metal folding table for off-road trips.  It is currently folded for easy transportation.
data.//: values based on real world collapsible camping table

data.description: A large sheet of leather.  You could use it as a picnic blanket, but it's more valuable as a surface for butchering as it does not soak up blood.  It's rolled and ready for carrying.

A large mat woven from fibrous material.  You could use it as a picnic blanket, but it's more valuable as a surface for butchering.  Too thin to be used as a comfortable sleeping mat.  It's rolled and ready for carrying.
A large wooden container used to turn raw milk into butter and buttermilk.  This model uses a foot crank and holds three gallons of raw milk.
A small water-powered mill that can convert starchy products into flour.  Needs to be placed via the construction menu.
A small wind-powered mill that can convert starchy products into flour.  Needs to be placed via the construction menu.
A large screw press for manually pressing oil out of fruit or seed paste.  Needs to be placed via the construction menu.
A massive bench-mounted device with a short guillotine blade mounted to a long lever.  Designed for making straight or curved cuts through sheet metal up to 3 millimeters thick.
data.//: Based on the Beverly B-2 Throatless Shear, 10 gauge capacity - as was furniture - values based on real world Beverly B-2 Throatless Shear

data.description: A floor-mounted machine containing all the levers, clamps, and mounts required to remove or fit a tire, plus an integrated foot pump to inflate it.
data.//: Based on the Redline TC500M Manual Tire Changer

data.description: A portable faceted reflector dish on a tripod, made of shaped metal panels that concentrate sunlight into a focal point for cooking.  Requires some assembly to set up and only works outdoors in strong direct sunlight.

Two steel plates mounted on a pipe in a double-sided oar design, installed in a sturdy frame with a rotating mechanism.  It spins when struck, eventually returning to vertical alignment due to one plate being heavier than the other.  You can use it for target practice when stationary targets become too easy.

use_action.done_message: You set up the spinner target, time to shoot!

data.description: A point-and-shoot digital camera with a digital viewfinder, a backup 'iron-sight', and flash.  You can look at your photos on the digital screen, or transfer them with any standard electronic device.
data.//: swappable, but proprietary 80g Li-Ion battery

data.description: A 35 mm digital SLR (single-lens reflex) camera with optical and digital viewfinders, a zoom lens with auto-focus and stabilizer, and flash.  You can look at your photos on the digital screen or transfer them with any standard electronic device.  Before the Cataclysm, you could have taken professional-grade photos using this.
data.//: swappable, but proprietary 160g Li-Ion battery

data.description: A cellphone, an older cousin of the smartphone that is still popular in certain circles due to its reliability and sturdiness.  Using the phone will turn it on and provide light, assuming it is sufficiently charged.  It also tells the time and has an alarm feature.
data.//: Nokia 105 4G, 26g Li-Ion battery

data.description: An antenna designed to pick up signals better when pointed at the source.  You could use this with a radio to receive faint signals.

A pair of electronic handcuffs, used by police and riot bots to detain captives.  Their continuous siren clearly identifies the wearer as an arrested criminal and alerts human police.  Wait for their arrival, don't try to escape or to remove the cuffs - they will administer an electric shock.
However, since the only police likely to respond are undead, you may have a long wait ahead, unless you get creative…
data.//: Don't add ELECTRONIC flag here, since these handcuffs have their own behavior when affected by EMP blast

data.description: A tablet PC using an efficient color e-ink display.  Before the Cataclysm, these were nifty gadgets; now, they are extremely useful tools.  Runs on conventional batteries.
data.//: amazon kindle, LIONX 6300mAh battery 42 ml
light 10 is the bare minimum for reading without penalties

data.description: A USB thumb drive.  Useful for holding electronic data.
data.//: Based on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B015CH1PJU

data.description: A USB thumb drive.  Maybe a decade out of date, but still useful for holding electronic data.
A portable external hard drive, the best in affordable mass storage.  Useful for holding lots of electronic data.
data.//: Based on https://www.amazon.com/Seagate-Portable-External-Hard-Drive/dp/B07CRG94G3

data.description: A memory card, can be used to store data.
A memory card.  Maybe a decade out of date, but can still be used to store data.

data.//: migrated, do not use and remove later

data.description: A memory card, can be used to store data.  This one has a label on which is written 'XEDRA' followed by a long string of numbers.
A bundle of electronics shielded in scrap metal.  It has an otherworldly connection for Exodii computers.
A bundle of electronics shielded in scrap metal.  It has an otherworldly connection for Exodii computers.  This one is filled with data downloaded from an Exodii computer.

data.//: Based on Panasonic Ranger 505
data.description: This looks like a travel TV from the 1970s, styled to resemble military field equipment.  The bulbous CRT is encased in a drab plastic shell with an oversized carrying handle.  The switches and chunky tuning controls look like they were salvaged from an abandoned Cold War command center.  A single camera lens is visible above the screen, slightly off center.

This device has many ports attached, allowing it to connect to almost any control panel or other electronic machine (but not computers).  With a little skill, it can be used to crack passwords and more.
data.//: hackrf one, + 300 ml for cables and antenna + slot for battery because real hackrf works from usb, not something we can emulate here

data.description: A tool for measuring radiation.  Using it will prompt you to choose whether to scan yourself or the terrain, or to turn on continuous scan, which will provide continuous feedback on ambient radiation.  It is currently off.
data.//: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0B541D433 but AA instead of 14500

data.description: A tool for measuring radiation.  It is in continuous scan mode, and will produce quiet clicking sounds in the presence of ambient radiation.  Using it allows you to turn it off, or scan yourself or the ground.

use_action.msg: The Geiger counter's SCANNING LED turns off.

data.description: This strange contraption appears to be little more than a laminated box built around a battery, a poorly backlit screen, and a wound spool of cloth netting.  The letters "X E D R A" are emblazoned on the side.  To operate the device, unfurl the netting and place it around the object to analyze.  Despite not appearing to do anything, it consumes an enormous amount of electricity and provides a brief numerical readout.
data.//: Battery only, intentionally. Meant for field expeditions to other dimensions where grid power is unavailable. Too advanced for the player to make grid-useable.

data.description: A strange apparatus, seemingly consisting of a glass-encased microphone linked to a small thermal printer and digital screen.  The screen remains perpetually blank, save for a battery indicator on its upper right, and on its left side lies a single red button: "PRINT DATA".
A hand-powered battery charger.  It has an adjustable receptacle designed to accept a wide variety of rechargeable battery cells.
A portable computer, a ubiquitous tool both before and after the cataclysm.  While you no longer have internet access, you still can load it with books and other useful software.
data.//: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D6Z664QC, battery is FRANGWAT01

data.description: This battery-powered device is loaded up with someone's music collection.  Fortunately, there's lots of songs you like, and listening to it will raise your morale slightly.  Use it to turn it on.
data.//: Sony NWE394 Walkman

use_action.message: You put in the earbuds and start listening to music.

data.description: This mp3 player is turned on and playing some great tunes, raising your morale steadily while on your person.  It runs through batteries quickly; you can turn it off by using it.  It also obscures your hearing.

use_action.message: You stop listening to music and take your earbuds out.

data.description: A device constructed by 'enhancing' a speaker with some amplifier circuits.  It has no other use besides emitting loud crackling static noise that could distract zombies.
A homemade device that is emitting horrible crackles, pops, and other loud static sounds.  Quick, get away from it before it draws zombies to you!

use_action.msg: The infernal racket dies as the noise emitter turns off.

data.//: Based off the TRIFIELD EMF Meter Model TF2.  Supposed to use 9volt, but uses medium battery instead
data.description: This device detects and reads out different electromagnetic wave lengths.  It beeps with proximity and is sensitive enough you could use it to get a sense of direction.
This device detects and reads out different wave lengths.  It is currently on, humming and beeping with proximity.  It is sensitive enough you could use it to get a sense of direction.
data.//: lasts 12 hours with backlight off

use_action.msg: The noise of your EMF detector slows to a halt.

data.description: A portable video game console, with a backlit screen allowing you to play in the dark.  You can use it to play a game, but this requires batteries.  Multiple game systems can be linked together for multiplayer games.
data.//: Nintendo Switch

data.description: A popular, fancy smartphone.  Capable of taking photos with its integrated camera and illuminating an area with its flashlight app, assuming it has enough charge.  The smartphone also has a clock app that includes an alarm and an app for tracking consumed calories.  Runs on a small, rechargeable power cell compatible with a Unified Power Supply.
data.//: stats from samsung galaxy s24

use_action.message: You put in the earbuds and start listening to music.

data.description: This phone is playing music, steadily raising your morale.  You can't hear anything else while you're listening.

use_action.message: You stop listening to music and take your earbuds out.

data.description: A popular, fancy smartphone.  Sadly for you, its previous user used its security features, rendering you unable to use most of its qualities.  You are still able to check the time and use a flashlight.  Runs on a small, rechargeable power cell compatible with a Unified Power Supply.

use_action.description: You can reset the smartphone to be able to use all its functions.

pocket_data.//: forbidden, so items still can spawn inside, but are not accessible by default.

data.description: A unified power supply, or UPS.  It is a device developed jointly by military and scientific interests for use in combat and the field.  The UPS is designed to power tools, smartphones, armor, and some guns, but drains batteries quickly.

A unified power supply, or UPS.  It is a device developed jointly by military and scientific interests for use in combat and the field.  The UPS is designed to power tools, smartphones, armor, and some guns, but drains batteries quickly.
data.//: Intended as an inverter that attaches to a battery, therefore it's volume will expand based on the size of battery attached.

data.description: A unified power supply, or UPS.  It is a device developed jointly by military and scientific interests for use in combat and the field.  The UPS is designed to power tools, smartphones, armor, and some guns, but drains batteries quickly.  Use it to turn it on.
data.//: Intended as an inverter that attaches to a battery, therefore it's volume will expand based on the size of battery attached.

data.description: A direct methanol fuel cell which can provide power to UPS-compatible electronic devices by oxidizing methanol supplied from a specialized fuel tank to produce electricity.
A vibrator.

variants.description: This truly multipurpose massage tool is just the thing you need to relax.  Use it to take a break and unwind.
This bulbous, u-shaped alien looking device will help you see the stars.  Use it to take a break and unwind.
You know what this is.  There's a switch at the bottom, you know what it's for.  Use it to take a break and unwind.

data.description: A compact thermoelectric generator.  Burns propane gas to charge UPS devices.  Use it to turn it on.
A compact thermoelectric generator.  When connected to a propane tank, it will slowly charge UPS-compatible devices.

This is a noisemaker that has been further enhanced with a series of amplifiers.  It's about as loud something can get without making you vomit from sound-induced nausea, and it's as sure to attract every zombie in town as it is to give you permanent hearing damage.
data.//: I estimate this thing is about 130 decibels.  Commercial amps can hit similar noise levels at a 100-200w of power input, the survivor's is less efficient.

data.description: This is a noisemaker that has been further enhanced with a series of amplifiers.  It's currently making an extraordinary amount of noise - hopefully you have hearing protection.

use_action.msg: The infernal racket dies as the noise emitter turns off.

sound_message.str: Your super noise emitter produces an unholy blast of sonic chaos.

data.description: A hefty prying tool.  Use it to open locked doors without destroying them, or to lift manhole covers.  You could also wield it to bash some heads in.
data.//1: With the assumption that it's a cylinder of 18in length and 1.5in diameter. Listing says 0.5in width BUT the crowbar itself is curved a little and package dimensions said 1.57in so I rounded it down slightly.
data.//2: Based on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07B4JDQB4

data.description: A pair of thin pieces of metal, one bent in an 'L' shape to push tumblers and the other acting as a torsion wrench.  These tools are almost totally inadequate for picking locks, but when you've got nothing else, it might work.
An improvised pick and torsion wrench made from scrap metal.  You'll need MacGyver-like skills to open locks with these as they are brittle, but they lower the chances of alarms being set off.
An ice axe with a hammer on the other end, a multi-purpose hiking and climbing tool used by mountaineers.  It is sturdy enough to lift manhole covers.

A pipe with both ends bent and hammered flat to resemble a crowbar.  Use it to open locked crates without destroying them, or to lift manhole covers.  It's not strong enough to pry doors or windows, though.  You could also wield it to fight with, in a pinch.
A locksmith's set of sturdy steel lockpicks and torsion wrenches.  It is essential for silently and quickly opening locks, provided you have some lockpicking and mechanical skills.

description.str: this a pseudo item

data.description: A 60-inch-long construction prybar.  Essentially a long, solid steel rod with a hardened chisel tip.
data.//1: With the assumption that it's a cylinder of 60in length and 1.5in diameter. Assuming 2.5in in diameter left it at 4l+ - item dimensions on the listing are yet again package dimensions that would inflate the volume.
data.//2: Based on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B007DHX596

A block of military-grade RDX composition explosive.  A label reads: "Highly explosive, use with extreme caution!" It comes with a small timer, which is currently ticking down.

data.description: This substantial device is a bomb that generates an electromagnetic pulse.  When activated, the plutonium fuel cell is drained into a flux compression generator, the detonation of which creates a strong magnetic field.  When this magnetic field is fed into the antenna, it creates a strong electro-magnetic pulse.

This EMP bomb is active and will shortly detonate, creating a large EMP field that damages robots and drains bionic energy, as well as a sizeable explosion.  You may not want to be holding it much longer.

A packed, disposable light anti-tank rocket launcher.  Once fired, it cannot be reloaded and must be disposed of.  Activate it to pop it out and make it ready to fire.

variants.description: The M72 LAW (Light Anti-armor Weapon) is a one-time use lightweight rocket launcher, meant to take out tanks and other armored vehicles.  Designed to replace the earlier Bazookas, it features a shaped-charge warhead to pierce armor.  Though weaker than the more modern and heavier AT4, it's still in service to this day.  Due to its design, you must unpack it to use it, and it cannot be reloaded.  Activate to unpack.

use_action.msg: You pull the activating lever, readying the LAW to fire.

data.//: This is based on the B54 Mod 1, all other man-portable nuclear weapons have far too high a yield.
data.description: The B54 Special Atomic Demolition Munition is an extremely powerful weapon, a portable nuclear bomb, using the smallest nuclear warhead in US inventory.  It is housed inside a extremely sturdy transit container.  Use it to activate the timer.  You guess that the explosion would be large enough to take out a small house.
The nuclear bomb looks no different from the outside, yet you know that the device is armed and counting down.  You should probably get far, far away from it.

data.description: A bottle of flammable liquid with a rag inserted.  Use this item to light the rag.  You will, of course, need a lighter or matches in your inventory to do this.  After lighting it, throw it to cause fires.
data.//COMMENT: The moves action cost should always be at least 100 (one full second) so that the molotov can properly know who's throwing it. See iuse::molotov_lit() for more details.

data.description: A bottle of flammable liquid with a flaming rag stoppered in its neck.  Throwing it will shatter the bottle on impact and ignite a fireball.  Dropping it will set you on fire, so don't do that unless you want to burn to death.
//: 2% chance per turn of going out harmlessly.
This is necessary to prevent a player from lighting a ton of molotovs and stuffing them in their backpack until pulling them out 6 weeks later.

data.description: An older brother of the generic Molotov cocktail, this wicked beverage uses thickened gasoline or straight napalm.  It, surprisingly, does not make for a fire of much higher temperature, but what it does is make the burning mixture ever more sticky.

data.description: A small hand press for hand loading firearm ammunition.  It comes with everything you need to start hand loading your own munitions.

A collection of items improvised for field reloading of shotshells.  A plank with a hole cut in the center, a medium-sized nail, and a whittled dowel are used to seat wads, decap primers, and (carefully!) reprime hulls.  Powder and shot are measured with a cut-down shotshell hull.  The opposite side of the plank has been shaped to allow for roll-crimping of the plastic hulls.  There's no provision for resizing, so reloaded hulls will fire best in the firearm they were fired from.
A tool used for properly disassembling firearm ammunition.
A small hand operated press, it can be used for staking, rivetting, or various other small jobs.  If you had a swage and die, you could use it to make copper jackets for handloading.
The internal tank for a gasoline fuel cell bionic.
The internal ethanol tank for an ethanol burner bionic.
The internal oil tank for an oil generator bionic.
The internal compartment for holding medium sized batteries, for a battery system bionic.
Integrated bionic tools implanted in your fingers.
Integrated bionic miniature welding tool implanted in your fingers.
Integrated bionic multimeter implanted in your fingers.
Integrated soldering iron and screwdriver set.

variants.description: A sharp knife designed for cutting meat.  It makes a poor melee weapon, but is decent at butchering corpses.
A short-bladed knife with a sharp blade, made for fine controlled cuts to vegetables without using a cutting board.

A long-bladed kitchen knife.  The blade is wider than the handle, giving room for the wielder's knuckles, and it has a characteristic curve for a fast rocking action for chopping vegetables.  It makes an acceptable melee weapon, but the wide blade is unwieldy for butchering.
A long-bladed kitchen knife with a thin, slightly curved blade for deftly slicing meat either in flat sheets or around the bone.  It makes a decent melee weapon, and is excellent for butchery.
This knife has quite a long blade with a scalloped edge for cutting bread.  It's not that sharp, but its length and heft mean it could do a bit of damage and cause some nasty tearing.
A sharp, heavy knife.  It makes a good melee weapon, and is an ideal item for butchering corpses.
A menacing-looking knife with a broad, square-shaped blade.  Its heft and sharpness would make it a very effective melee weapon and an excellent butchering tool.
A menacing-looking knife with a broad, square shaped blade, curved for fast vegetable chopping.  Its heft and sharpness make it a decent weapon as well, although not as good as a meat cleaver.

data.description: A knife made of crudely-worked copper with a simple handle.  Primitive, but a step above stone-age.
A cast bronze knife with a full tang, with a handle wrapped in cord and leather, lovingly work-hardened and sharpened to a fine edge.

data.//: Too small to be effectively used for butchering, still not bad at it due to serrated edge.
data.description: A short, sturdy knife with a serrated edge for cutting lines and straps, and a blunt tip for prying.  Used primarily by divers, this knife has been fitted with cork to slow its descent if dropped underwater, so it takes up more space than usual.
A sharp, knife-like tool used for harvesting honey from beehives.  Makes a passable melee weapon.
A small pocket knife.  It isn't great for combat, but it's better than nothing.  It's sharp enough to butcher with.
A sharpened stone set into a hollowed handle.  Not nearly as usable as a proper knife, but it's better than nothing.
A small knife designed for opening boxes.  It could cause some damage, but it really should be used against inanimate objects.  It is too small to effectively butcher corpses with.
A rock with sharpened edges, produced by knapping.  Works as a crude cutting and butchering tool, if nothing else is available.
A large stick with the end carved into a broad blade for digging.  It could be used to dig shallow pits, but not deep ones.
A small, sharp gardening shovel, perfect for digging up grubs and worms.
A farming implement.  You can use it to turn tillable land into a slow-to-cross pile of dirt, or dig a shallow pit.
A farming implement made from bronze.  The added heft and durability should let you till soil for farming more easily as well.

A crude shovel with a shovelhead made from wood, historically used as an alternative to metal shovels when metal was too expensive.  It works passably well, but really can't compare to a metal shovel.
A sturdy metal rake, a must-have during autumn.
A cheap plastic rake.  Will break quite quickly if used for anything other than raking leaves.
An old-fashioned farming tool used to cut tall grass.  Despite being a giant blade on the end of a stick, it is incredibly awkward to use for anything but its intended purpose.
A dull, cheaply-made replica of an old-fashioned farming tool used to cut tall grass.
A long, crooked tool used to reap souls, with a skull engraved in its blade.  Let the harvest begin.
A digging tool.  Use it to dig pits adjacent to your location.
A sturdy metal shovel used for picking up snow and moving it somewhere else.  It was useful before the Cataclysm, but now it's useless.
A cheap plastic shovel used for picking up snow and moving it somewhere else.  It was useful before the Cataclysm, but now it's useless.
A primitive tool for cutting grass.  The sharp, crescent-shaped stone at the end of the handle is barely good enough for the job.
An old-fashioned farming tool for cutting tall grass.  Despite being a massive curved blade on a handle, it is incredibly awkward to use for anything but its intended purpose.
A handheld grass-cutting tool with a cast bronze blade, fastened to a wood handle wrapped with leather.
A slightly curved steel blade with a nice wooden handle, not too dissimilar to a machete.
The steel curved blade of a bill placed stoutly on top an axe handle.  It still isn't long enough to use as a spear, but it'll still cleave your enemies.
A long, slightly curved steel blade on the end of a sturdy shaft.  Could be used to thoroughly ruin something's day, or cut branches and small trees.
The bronze curved blade of a bill placed stoutly atop an axe handle.  It still isn't long enough to use as a spear, but it'll still cleave your enemies.
A slightly curved bronze blade with a nice wooden handle, not too dissimilar to a machete.
A long, slightly curved and hooked bronze blade on the end of a sturdy shaft.  Could be used to thoroughly ruin something's day, or cut branches and small trees.

Due to the instability of ketene, it can't be stored and must be used immediately.
A kit with hundreds of pieces and dozens of blueprints for small engineering projects designed for beginner learners.  Explore mechanics and hydraulics!

A complete robotics engineering system, for learning the basics of building and programming robots.  Using sensors, motors, a core controller, and hundreds of snap-together building pieces, you can follow the instructions to assemble 12 different robots.  The versatile parts also allow you to make robots according to your own designs.
A Stirling engine kit that demonstrates the principles behind the generation of electricity through the use of hot air.
A small 0.9 cubic foot vacuum oven used to purge residual solvents out of liquids and solids.  Looks kind of like a microwave.

A small closed loop extractor used for extracting essential oils from organic material, producing a high quality-extract.  It consists of a long metal tube clamped onto a steel "honey pot".  Organic material is packed in the tube, flushed with solvent, and essential oils gathered from the pot.  Must be powered up to operate.

A large machine used for extracting essential oils from large batches of organic material, producing a low-quality crude oil.  It consists of three long metal tubes funneled into a large drum that's set horizontally.  A series of hoses and tubes come out of the machine going to different valves.  It needs to be powered up to operate.

A makeshift extraction system.  It's pretty much just a 55 gallon drum, a pipe to stir the solution, and a faucet at the bottom to drain the extractor.  Not the most ideal piece of equipment, but it will work.

A makeshift extraction system, or as makeshift as you can consider something that was purpose-built in a laboratory by a group of experts.  Meticulously disassembled.  You can reassemble and plug it into your own power grid to use it.

A piece of filter paper for separating solids from liquids.  This filter paper has a rating of 2 microns, separating more solids out than quantitative filter paper, but the process takes longer.  It's intended to be disposable, but you could probably use it for some time before it's unusable.

A piece of filter paper for separating solids from liquids.  This filter paper has a rating of 20 microns, separating less solids out than qualitative filter paper, but the process is much faster.  It's intended to be disposable, but you could probably use it for some time before it's unusable.
A set of three plastic gaskets.  They're intended to be single-use, but you could probably use it for some time before they're too worn out to use.
A small belt-driven mechanical pump capable of achieving a vacuum of -29.99 hg (50 microns).
A medium-sized vacuum pump designed to recover solvent (hydrocarbons) from extracted essential oils.
A makeshift appliance which decomposes water into oxygen and hydrogen via electrolysis of sodium hydroxide solution.  Much less energy-efficient than actual industrial equipment.
data.//: Energy efficiency is 40%, consuming 355 MJ and 8.936 L of water for 1 kg of H2 and 7.936 kg of O2.

data.description: A huge appliance built from salvaged industrial equipment, which produces ammonia via the Haber-Bosch process from hydrogen and nitrogen.  As it uses primitive catalysts for the reaction, energy efficiency is very low.  This one is powered by electricity.
data.//: Consumes 200 MJ for 1 kg of NH3.

data.description: A rather complicated system of thick-walled pipes, powerful compressors, and wiring, meant to interface with a reactor producing ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen via Haber-Bosch process.  It also acts as a power source for all the low-powered electrical components of the system.
data.//: Consumes 20 MJ for 1 kg of NH3.

data.description: A large makeshift appliance which captures nitrogen from the air for use in chemistry projects.  It includes a standard air filter for filtering out dust and other large particles, a deliquescent dryer to remove water vapor from air, and a nitrogen membrane filter to separate nitrogen from dry air.
data.//: Uses up 1.2 MJ for 1 m^3 of N2 (1.253 kg), assuming 99.5% purity.

data.description: A large yellow case filled with equipment to measure atmospheric conditions.  It is outfitted with a carrying handle, a telescoping stand, and a rechargeable battery pack.  Its small display can show the current weather.  It can also make long-term recordings, but these data are useless without specialized software to interpret them.

data.description: A sleek black case housing a mix of mundane and otherworldly devices that can be deployed from the top of the box.  It is also equipped with a built-in analysis computer, a small thermal printer, and a rechargeable battery.  The case itself is outfitted with back straps and a telescoping stand.  "X.E.D.R.A." and "HE weather station" are engraved on the case.

A brown and white case housing equipment to measure atmospheric conditions in extremely hazardous environments.  It is equipped with several deployable sensors, a Hub 01 NRE recorder, a built-in analysis computer, a thermal printer, and a rechargeable battery.  The case itself is outfitted with back straps and a telescoping stand.  The Hub 01 logo is displayed proudly on the case lid.
A tank of compressed nitrogen gas.  Nitrogen is useful for its lack of reactivity.  Don't try to breathe it.

A metal grille with a layer of platinum plating, suitable for use as a catalyst for some chemical reactions.
A rare, bizarre, and arcane device of an otherworldly nature.  It's giving you a headache just looking at it.  It is covered in alien markings.

data.description: An experimental device that will teleport you a short distance when activated.

A hefty kit containing some basic things you should probably not try to do precise chemistry without: a small balance scale, a spectrophotometer, cuvettes, a melting point apparatus, a pH meter, and a set of paper for thin layer chromatography.  This makes it a lot easier to feel confident that the chemical you've made is what you think it is.
A simple scale that uses a set of steel weights on sliding bars to measure a sample's mass quite accurately.
A ubiquitous analytical chemistry tool that measures the light absorption of a liquid sample in a special tube called a cuvette.
A small box filled with precisely-calibrated square plastic tubes for laboratory spectrometer use.
A pair of glass probes attached to a voltmeter.  By putting one probe into a calibration solution (conveniently included) and the other in a substance, you can calculate the substance's acidity.
A device with two probes that let you measure the electrical potential between two points.

A gadget that is a little bigger than a handheld calculator, with a digital display and two pointed probes connected by wires.  It can measure not just voltage, but current in amps, and resistance in ohms, as well as test for electrical continuity.
data.//: Dimensions from a sampling of consumer digital multimeter models online.

data.description: A hot plate with a metal housing attached.  The metal housing has a magnification viewport and a slot into which a capillary tube containing a crystallized sample is inserted.  The device lets you precisely measure the melting point of a crystal, a property very useful in identifying what it is and how pure it is.

A small, hefty, boring-looking machine.  Its weighted trapezoidal frame has a single on-off switch and a speed dial, and on top of it sits a rubber receptacle.  Pressing a test tube into the receptacle would, with power, rapidly shake and mix the contents of the test tube.  It's surprisingly fun to use.
A photodiode on a chip, designed to convert incoming light to electrical energy for quantification.
A high-quality crystal glass prism for separating and redirecting light.
A small glass tube.  Small, tube-shaped, and made of glass.
data.//: Volume here is displacement volume of a corked 25mL test tube.

data.description: A classic tool for the ages!  This hefty, durable piece of lab equipment makes small things look bigger.  When powered, it allows the user to observe various samples on a microscopic scale.

This microscope has less magnification than a standard one.  It's also stereoscopic and produces a neat 3-D image of the surface.  It was typically used for performing dissections and other fine-detail work on small creatures.  It still works pretty well with an added light source, but what would you do with it?

This thing doesn't look much like a funnel.  It's a teardrop-shaped piece of glass with a stopper at the wide end and a valve at the other.  It can be used to wash one liquid with another, like water and an oil, and then draw off whichever of the two liquids contains a higher amount of whatever compound you're trying to isolate.  With a high level of skill, it can also be used to make juvenile farting noises.
A tall glass column with a stopcock at the end.  If you're serious about chemistry, you probably have a tattoo of one of these somewhere.

Just looking at this thing makes you feel like a proper mad scientist.  It's a series of glass tubes and round flasks, connected to a central motor and a heating element.  The heating element warms one flask, kept rotating by the motor, evaporating the contents.  The vapor is then condensed in the tubes and collected in another flask, in case you wanted to save it for later.

One of the classic pieces of mad science glassware, this is a small-volume still that passes vapor through a fractional distillation column and then condenses the distillate in a cooled collection column.  A grad student or a robot (is there really any difference?) collects the distillate in fractions so that specific contents can be analyzed.  Going a few milliliters at a time, it would not be very effective to try to distill whiskey in this thing.

A set of plastic trays, electrodes, and a power supply designed to create an electric voltage gradient through a liquid solution containing a solid gel.  Stuff like proteins and DNA would then get separated on the gel according to electrical charge and size.  Pretty useless now for anything but salvage.

A smaller, benchtop version of the larger furniture-sized centrifuge.  Don't be fooled by its portable scale; it's still a very powerful piece of equipment that can spin stuff really quickly.  It's not a toy!

data.//: based on https://www.eppendorf.com/ae-en/Products/Centrifugation/High-Speed-Centrifuges/High-Speed-Centrifuge-CR30NX-p-PF-923312

Stop giggling.  This is a tiny plastic valve, get your mind out of the gutter.
A plastic box with holes in it.  Not that exciting, unless you're desperate for a place to store a test tube.  Then it's great.
A plastic tray riddled with small holes, for storing microcentrifuge tubes.
A heavy metal plate and a sturdy rod, for clamping lab stuff to.

data.description: Also called storm glass or 'Goethe barometer', The weather glass barometer consists of a glass container with a sealed body, half filled with water.  A narrow spout connects to the body below the water level and rises above the water level.  The difference between the sealed water level in the body and the narrow open spout determines the atmospheric pressure.  Activate to get current atmospheric pressure.

armor.//: The cotton represents the head harness that keeps the mask attached to one's melon. Hood-style masks, like the GP5, should get their own item.
While some older gas masks had lenses made from glass, most modern ones are fabricated with plastic eyepieces or visors. We can hand-wave away the outliers.
The exhale valve, speech diaphragm, and, if a mask has them, the communications unit and drinking tube, are located over the mouth and nose sections. They're represented by the plastic content.
Most modern gas masks possess plastic filter mounts on either one or both of the cheek sections, which this plastic represents. Again, we can tactically handwave away the outliers.
