data.dynamic_line: I'm the most senior member at this point, so I'm what passes for the leader here now.  I'm just trying to make plans to keep us alive since everything fell apart.

Well, that's a long story.  We are what's left of the Grey Moose militia.  We had plans for when things went south cause of crazy politicians or war, but we didn't expect people to go crazy then turn zombie.  Only a handful of our members actually made it through all that madness.  What's worse is that we lost so much of our supplies and gear due to military checkpoints and trigger happy soldiers.  It didn't matter that half of us were former military, the checkpoint guards just saw weapons, panicked and then confiscated everything but the clothes on our back.  So here we are, at our planned escape location, with not even a fraction of our manpower or supplies.

I can't say I can think of anything at the moment.  Our remoteness is our defense.  We want to keep a low profile and try to keep out of any trouble in this isolated location.  We are willing to trade for weapons and ammo though.  Keeping the nearby area clear and hunting is always eating away at our supplies.

responses.text: Keeping a low profile is good.

data.dynamic_line: Let's trade then.
Stay safe out there.  Not enough of us are around anymore.

dialogue.describe: You wouldn't believe what I found…
dialogue.offer: Holy hell, the crash you recovered the black box from wasn't as old as I thought.  Check this out, it was on its approach to pick up a team sent to secure and destroy something called a 'Hazardous Waste Sarcophagus' in the middle of nowhere.  If the bird never picked up the team then we may still have a chance to meet up with them.  It includes an access code for the elevator and an encoded message for the team leader, I guess.  If we want to join up with what remains of the government then now may be our only chance.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck ya, America!
dialogue.rejected: Are you going to forfeit your duty when the country needs you the most?
dialogue.advice: If there is a military team down there then we better go in prepared if we want to impress them.  Carry as much ammo as you can and prepare to ditch this place if they have a second bird coming to pick them up.
dialogue.inquire: Having any trouble following the map?  Remember to search underground.
dialogue.success: Maybe these things are what remains of the team we were searching for…
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I oughta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, we were so close.

dialogue.offer: I'm asthmatic.  I need you to get an inhaler for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank god, thank you so much!  I won't last more than a couple of days, so hurry…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, I'll be dead soon without your help!
dialogue.advice: There's a town nearby.  Check pharmacies; it'll be in the back with the good stuff.
dialogue.success: Oh thank god!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.describe: This infection is bad, totally bad…
dialogue.offer: I'm infected.  Badly.  I need you to get some good antibiotics for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank god, thank you so much!  I won't last more than a couple of days, so hurry…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, I'll be dead soon without your help!
dialogue.advice: There's a town nearby.  Check pharmacies; it'll be in the back, either antibiotics or broad-spectrum antibiotics will do.
dialogue.success: Oh thank god!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.describe: We've got the flag, now we need to locate US forces.
dialogue.offer: We have the flag but now we need to locate US troops to see what we can do to help.  I haven't seen any but I'm figurin' one of those choppers that were flyin' round during th' outbreak would have a good idea.  If you can get me a black box from one of the wrecks I'll look into where we might open 'er at.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck yeah, America!
dialogue.rejected: Do you have any better ideas?
dialogue.advice: Survivors were talkin' 'bout seeing 'em falling out of the sky but I don't know where.  If I were a pilot I'd avoid crash landing in a city or forest though.  Black boxes are housed in the tail to survive the crash so check there when you do find one.  Now get to it!
dialogue.success: America, fuck yeah!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I oughta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, I'll have to find 'er myself.

dialogue.describe: With the black box in hand, we need to find a lab.
dialogue.offer: Thanks to your searching we've got the black box but now we need to have a look inside her.  Now, most buildings don't have power anymore but there are a few that might be of use.  Have you ever seen one of those science labs that have popped up in the middle of nowhere?  Them suckers have a glowing terminal out front so I know they have power somewhere inside 'em.  If you can get inside and find a computer lab that still works you ought to be able to find out what's in the black box.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck yeah, America!
dialogue.rejected: Do you have any better ideas?
dialogue.advice: When I was playin' with the terminal for the one I ran into it kept asking for an ID card.  Finding one would be the first order of business.
dialogue.success: America, fuck yeah!  I was in the guard a few years back so I'm confident I can make heads-or-tails of these transmissions.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I oughta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, I maybe we can find an egg-head to crack the terminal.

dialogue.offer: I hope you will find use from what you got out of the deposit box but I also have another job for you that might lead you to an opportunity to deal out justice for those who cannot.  First things first, we can't just look like ruffians.  Find us a deputy badge, easy enough?
dialogue.accepted: I'd check the police station.
dialogue.rejected: We're also official… just hang in there and I'll show you what we can really do.
dialogue.advice: They shouldn't be that hard to find… should they?
dialogue.success: Great work, Deputy.  We're in business.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the criminals if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: Does our flag still yet wave?
dialogue.offer: Does our flag still yet wave?  We're battered but not yet out of the fight, we need the old colors!
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya!  Find me one of those big ol' American flags.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  God damned commie…
dialogue.advice: Find a large federal building or school, they must have one.
dialogue.success: America, fuck ya!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: You give up?  This country fell apart because no one could find a good man to rely on… might as well give up, I guess.

dialogue.offer: Our world fell apart because our leaders were as crooked as the con-men that paid for their elections.  Just find me one of those corporate accounting books and I'll show you and the rest of the world just who is at fault.
dialogue.accepted: You'll see, I know I'm right.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but the big corporations didn't get a chance to destroy the evidence yet.
dialogue.advice: Try a big corporate building of some sort, they're bound to have an accounting department.
dialogue.success: Great, let's see… uh… hmmm….  Fine, I didn't even do my own taxes but I'm sure this will prove their guilt if we get an expert to examine it.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the corporations if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: I hope I don't see many names I know…
dialogue.offer: I've lost so many friends… please find me a patient list from the regional hospital or doctor's office.  I just want to know who might still be out there.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, I suppose it won't change what has already happened but it will bring me closure.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just want to know what happened to everyone.
dialogue.advice: I bet you'll run into a lot of those things in the hospital, please be careful.
dialogue.success: Oh dear, I thought Timmy would have made it…
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

dialogue.describe: I wonder if a retreat might exist…
dialogue.offer: Everyone who dies gets back up, right?  Which means that whatever is causing this it must be airborne to have infected everyone.  I believe that if that is the case then there should be regions that were not downwind from where-ever the disease was released.  We need to find a record of all the weather patterns leading up to the outbreak.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks so much, you may save both of us yet.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: I'm not sure, maybe a news station would have what we are looking for?
dialogue.success: These look more complicated than I thought, just give me some time.
dialogue.success_lie: This isn't what we need.
dialogue.failure: If only we could find a great valley or something.

dialogue.describe: Any variant is fine, I am not that choosy…
dialogue.offer: The sky has torn apart and creatures beyond our wildest imaginations lurk in the dark now.  I beg you, find me a holy symbol.  Maybe some faith can help me sleep better at night.
dialogue.accepted: May whatever god or spirits that now reign the world protect you.
dialogue.rejected: I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: A church must be full of them and who knows, maybe some of those <zombies> carry some.  But please, do not waste your time making one yourself.
dialogue.inquire: Any luck?  Please find me a holy symbol.  Any of them will do.
dialogue.success: Thank the heavens.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do me?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Find a relic of a forgotten saint.  Places like <color_yellow>cathedrals</color> or <color_yellow>museums</color> might have one.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: As the world seems to abandon the reality that we once knew, it becomes plausible that the old superstitions that were cast aside may have had some truth to them.  Please go and find me a religious relic… I doubt it will be of much use but I've got to hope in something.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I suppose a large church or cathedral may have something.
dialogue.inquire: Any luck?  Please find me a small relic.  Any relic will do.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I need some time alone now…
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: Now I don't mean to upset you but I'm not sure what I can do with the accounting ledger at the moment.  We do have a new lead though, the ledger has a safe deposit box under the regional manager's name.  Guess what, dumb sucker wrote down his combination.  Come with me to retrieve the box and you can keep any of the goodies in it that I can't use to press charges against these bastards.
dialogue.accepted: You may make a tidy profit from this.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but the world is going to be just as corrupt when we start rebuilding unless we take measure to stop those who seek to rule over us.
dialogue.advice: This shouldn't be hard unless we run into a horde.
dialogue.success: Great, anything I can't use to prosecute the bastards is yours, as promised.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the corporations if it hasn't already.

data.description: Retrieve the software in their computer marked on your map.

dialogue.describe: Oh man, I can't believe I forgot to download it…
dialogue.offer: There's some important software on my computer that I need on USB.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks!  Just pull the data onto this USB drive and bring it to me.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  It's an easy job…
dialogue.advice: Take this USB drive.  Use the console, and download the software.
dialogue.inquire: So, do you have my software yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent, thank you!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: Wow, you failed?  All that work, down the drain…

dialogue.describe: It could be very informative to perform an analysis of zombie blood…
dialogue.offer: I need someone to get a sample of zombie blood, take it to a hospital, and perform a centrifuge analysis of it.
dialogue.accepted: Excellent.  Take this blood draw kit; once you've produced a zombie corpse, use it to extract blood from the body, then take it to a hospital for analysis.
dialogue.rejected: Are you sure?  The scientific value of that blood data could be priceless…
dialogue.advice: The centrifuge is a bit technical; you might want to study up on the usage of computers before completing that part.
dialogue.inquire: Well, do you have the data yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent!  This may be the key to removing the infection.
dialogue.success_lie: Wait, you couldn't possibly have the data!  Liar!
dialogue.failure: What a shame, that data could have proved invaluable…

data.description: Investigate the strange cabin in the woods and find an item that may clue you in about <color_yellow>a potential human sacrifice</color> the cult has performed, such as <color_yellow>human bones or other remains</color>.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: You have no idea how interesting this diary is.  I have two very promising leads… first things first, the Catholic Church has been performing its own investigations into global cult phenomenon and it appears to have become very interested in a local cult as of recently.  Could you investigate a location for me?  I'm not sure what was going on here but the priest seemed fairly worried about it.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path… You may need it this time more than the past excursions you have gone on.  There is a note about potential human sacrifice in the days immediately before and after the outbreak.  The name of the cult is believed to be the Church of Starry Wisdom but it is noted that accounts differ.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I doubt the site is still occupied but I'd carry a firearm at least… I'm not sure what you might be looking for but I'm positive you'll find something out of the ordinary if you look long enough.
dialogue.inquire: I'm positive there is something there… there has to be, any luck?
dialogue.success: Thank you, your account of these… demonic creations proves the fears the churches had were well founded.  Our priority should be routing out any survivors of this cult… I don't known if they are responsible for the outbreak but they certainly know more about it than I do.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: I have another task if you are feeling up to it.  There is a prisoner that the priest made special mention of.  I was wondering if you could see what may have happened to him or if he left anything in his cell.  The priest admits the individual is rather unstable, to put it lightly, but the priest personally believed the man was some kind of repentant visionary.  I'm not in a position to cast out the account just yet… it seems the man has prophesied events accurately before concerning the Church of Starry Wisdom.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path… I can only imagine that the prison will be a little slice of hell.  I'm not sure what they would have decided to do with the inmates when they knew death was almost certain.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: The worst case scenario will probably be that the prisoners have escaped their cells and turned the building into their own little fortress.  Best case, the building went into lock-down and secured the prisoners in their cells.  Either way, navigating the building will pose its own difficulties.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I'm not sure what to make of this but I'll ponder your account.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: Well damn, you must be the guys here to pick me up…
dialogue.offer: I got the brief so I know what I'm getting into.  Let me be upfront, treat me like shit and I'm going to cover my own hide.  However, you treat me well and give me something to believe in, even if it's just a shiny bit of metal, and I'll do you right.  Without a strong band a man doesn't stand a chance in this world.  You ready to take charge boss?  This world could use a Sheriff just about now.
dialogue.accepted: Before we get into a major fight just make sure we have the gear we need, boss.
dialogue.rejected: I don't think you're going to find many other survivors who haven't taken up a faction yet.
dialogue.advice: I'm a pretty good shot with a rifle or pistol.
dialogue.success: Wait… are you really making me a deputy?
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think so…
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: You seem to know this new world better than most…
dialogue.offer: You're kitted out better than most… would you be interested in making this world a little better for the rest of us?  The towns have enough supplies for us survivors to start securing a foothold but we don't have anyone with the skills and equipment to thin the masses of undead.  I'll lend you a hand to the best of my ability but you really showed promise taking out that other beast.  You, I, and a 100 zombies laid to rest, what do you say?
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya, we may get ourselves killed but we'll be among the first legends of the apocalypse.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either… but then I remember that most of us survivors won't make it unless someone decides to take the initiative.
dialogue.advice: I'd secure an ammo cache and try to sweep a town in multiple passes.
dialogue.success: Man… you're a goddamn machine.  It was a pleasure working with you.  You know, you may just change our little neck of the world if you keep this up.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think that was quite a hundred dead zeds.
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: I've heard some bad rumors so I hope you are up for another challenge…
dialogue.offer: Apparently one of the other survivors picked up on an unusually dense horde of undead moving into the area.  At the center of this throng there was a 'leader' of some sort.  The short of it is, kill the son of a bitch.  We don't know what it is capable of or why it is surrounded by other zombies but this thing reeks of trouble.  Do whatever it takes but we can't risk it getting away.
dialogue.accepted: I'll lend you a hand but I'd try and recruit another gunslinger if you can.
dialogue.rejected: What's the use of walking away, they'll track you down eventually.
dialogue.advice: Don't risk torching the building it may be hiding in if it has a basement.  The sucker may still be alive under the rubble and ash.
dialogue.success: May that bastard never get up again.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think we got it yet.
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: The eater of the dead… something was ripping zombies to shreds and only leaving a few scattered limbs…
dialogue.offer: A few days ago another survivor and I were trying to avoid the cities by staying in the woods during the day and foraging for gear at night.  It worked well against the normal zeds but one night something caught onto our trail and chased us for ten minutes or so until we decided to split up and meet-up back here.  My buddy never showed up and I don't have the means to kill whatever it was.  Can you lend a hand?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, make sure you're ready for whatever the beast is.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either.
dialogue.advice: I'd carry a shotgun at least, it sounded pretty big.
dialogue.success: You look a little shaken up, I can't tell you how glad I am that you killed it though.
dialogue.success_lie: Something in the shadows still seems to stare at me when I look at the woods.
dialogue.failure: I'm glad you came back alive… I wasn't sure if I had sent you to your death.

dialogue.describe: Oh god, I can't believe it happened…
dialogue.offer: My mom… she's… she was killed, but then she just got back up… she's one of those things now.  Can you put her out of her misery for me?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you… she would've wanted it this way.
dialogue.rejected: Please reconsider, I know she's suffering…
dialogue.advice: Find a gun if you can, make it quick…
dialogue.inquire: Well…?  Did you… finish things for my mom?
dialogue.success: Thank you.  I couldn't rest until I knew that was finished.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Really… that's too bad.

dialogue.describe: I just need a place to start over…
dialogue.offer: I've accepted that everyone I used to know is dead… one way or another.  I really wish I could have done something to save my brother but he was one of the first to go.  I'd like to start over, just rebuild at one of the farms in the countryside.  Can you help me secure one?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, let's find a remote one so we don't have to worry about many zombies.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just don't know what to do otherwise.
dialogue.advice: Traveling the backroads would be a good way to search for one.
dialogue.inquire: Shall we keep looking for a farm house?
dialogue.success: Well, my adventuring days are over.  I can't thank you enough.  Trying to make this place self sustaining will take some work but the future is looking brighter.  At least it ought to be safe for now.  You'll always be welcome here.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I guess it was just a pipe dream.

dialogue.describe: Maybe they escaped to one of the camps…
dialogue.offer: I can't thank you enough for bringing me the patient records but I do have another request.  You seem to know your way around… could you take me to one of the FEMA camps?  I know some were overrun but I don't want to believe all of them could have fallen.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, just bring me to the camp… I just want to see.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I don't know what else to do.
dialogue.advice: We should go at night, if it is overrun then we can quickly make our escape.
dialogue.inquire: Any leads on where a camp might be?
dialogue.success: I guess this wasn't as bright an idea as I thought.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

data.description: Find something that may reveal what the church's stance is on these events.  Something like <color_yellow>a priest's diary</color> would suffice.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: From what I understand, the creatures you encountered surrounding this relic were unlike anything I've heard of.  It is laughable that I now consider the living dead to be part of our ordinary reality.  Never-the-less, the church must have some explanation for these events.  I have located the residence of a local clergy man, could you go to this address and recover any items that may reveal what the church's stance is on these events?
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: If the information is confidential the priest must have it hidden within his own home.
dialogue.success: Thank you, a diary is exactly what I was looking for.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Go to the cabin in the woods where the Tracker is camping and <color_yellow>recruit them</color>.

dialogue.describe: You seem to know this new world better than most…
dialogue.offer: We've got another problem to deal with but I don't think we can handle it on our own.  So, I sent word out and found us a volunteer… of sorts.  He's vain as hell but has a little skill with firearms.  He was supposed to collect whatever he had of value and is going to meet us at a cabin in the woods.  Wasn't sure how long we were going to be so I told him to just camp there until we picked him up.
dialogue.accepted: Roger, if he's a no-show then any other gunslinger will do… but I doubt he'll quit before we even begin.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either… but then I remember that most of us survivors won't make it unless someone decides to take the initiative.
dialogue.advice: I hope the bastard is packing heat… else we'll need to grab him a gun before we hit our next target.
dialogue.success: Great, just let me know when you are ready to wade knee-deep in an ocean of blood.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think so…
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.offer: I left my poor dog in a house, not far from here.  Can you retrieve it?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you!  Please hurry back!
dialogue.rejected: Please, think of my poor little puppy!
dialogue.advice: Take my dog whistle; if the dog starts running off, blow it and he'll return to your side.
dialogue.inquire: Have you found my dog yet?
dialogue.success: Thank you so much for finding him!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Oh no!  My poor puppy…

name.str: Break into armory to retrieve family photo

dialogue.describe: I need you to get my family photo from the armory safe.
dialogue.offer: I left the only photo I have from my family in the armory.  I don't have the code, can you get in?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, it's great to see someone willing to help a out.
dialogue.rejected: Well, I'll find someone else to do it for me, real shame with all those guns locked up too…
dialogue.advice: You look like a resourceful sort, maybe you can hack it or something.
dialogue.inquire: Got the photo?  Should've been in my gun safe.
dialogue.success: Thanks!  I'll be sure to put in a good word for you around town.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand it over.
dialogue.failure: Shit happens.

data.description: Prove your dedication to the Foodperson and Foodplace as a whole by finding <color_yellow>10 Foodplace loyalty cards</color>.

dialogue.offer: Show me the proof of your loyalty to the great Foodplace, and I'll consider you worthy of my friendship.  Ten loyalty cards should be enough, I'm sure you already have much more than that waiting for you at home, right?
dialogue.accepted: That's the spirit!  Good luck kid.
dialogue.rejected: That's alright not everyone is cutout for this.
dialogue.advice: Those are very precious, people would probably keep them on their person or in bank vaults.  And definitely not throw them in the trash!
dialogue.inquire: How is it going?  Do you have them?
dialogue.success: YES!  I knew you could do it!  You proved your worth and I'm proud to call you a friend.
dialogue.success_lie: Well… where are they?
dialogue.failure: I'm so disappointed in you kid…

data.description: Prove you're a survivor by surviving for 10 days after the Cataclysm, and then returning to the person who gave you this mission.

dialogue.describe: It's hard to tell who actually has the skills to survive these days…
dialogue.offer: It's hard surviving out here on our own, and we'd probably have a better chance working together.  Problem is, I don't really know you and what you're capable of.  You might have what it takes, or you might not.  Either way, I'm going to need some proof.  Come back in a few days and I'll gladly follow you.  It's basically a win-win for me: either you come back and I'll know you've got what it takes, or you don't and I'll know that I was right not to follow you.
dialogue.accepted: I'll see you then… or I won't, and then I'll know I made the right decision.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: Don't die.  If you're asking me for advice, that doesn't bode well for you.
dialogue.success: I'll be honest, I wasn't really expecting to see you again.  A promise is a promise, I'll follow you now!
dialogue.success_lie: I know time is relative and all that.
dialogue.failure: I'm not quite sure how you failed to survive AND are talking to me.

name.str: Gather cattail stalks to create cattail jelly

data.description: Gather <color_yellow>60 cattail stalks</color> from the swamp and bring them back to <color_light_red>learn how to craft cattail jelly</color>.  Raise your <color_yellow>survival skill to at least 1</color> by harvesting cattail stalks.  <color_yellow>Bring back the provided bag with the 60 cattail stalks in them</color> as well.

effect.u_message: You learn how to craft cattail jelly.

dialogue.describe: Medical services are a little sparse following <the_cataclysm>, but people have been surviving using their wits and the bounty of Mother Nature for a long time.  Care to learn a little?
dialogue.offer: Did you know that cattails are a source of a jelly that works as an antiseptic and analgesic?  Something like that is likely to be mighty helpful out here.  I want you to take this bag, head to the nearest swamp, collect 60 cattail stalks, and bring them back here.  In exchange, I'll show you how to harvest the jelly.
dialogue.accepted: Great!  <color_yellow>This bag should be big enough to hold all of the stalks we'll need.  Don't forget to bring it back.</color>
dialogue.rejected: Your loss.
dialogue.advice: The cattails grow in the fresh water in swamps.  You can't miss them.
dialogue.inquire: Got those cattail stalks yet?  Don't forget to <color_yellow>bring back my bag with the stalks in them</color> and to work on improving your survival skill as well.
dialogue.success: Great!  Hand them over and I'll show you how this works.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand them over.
dialogue.failure: Well, that's a shame.

data.description: Bring the pyromaniac to <color_light_blue>their rival's house</color> and don't forget to <color_yellow>bring at least 200 units of gasoline</color>.  After you got there, talk to the pyromaniac to start burning the house.

dialogue.describe: Oh man, I want to fucking burn it so bad…
dialogue.offer: I'm so fucking infuriated!  I've got an enemy that ruined my life, and now I want to get revenge!  I don't care about <the_cataclysm>, I just want to burn his house!  Would you help me, <name_g>?
dialogue.accepted: Good.  Let's go to his house and goddamn burn it down!  Oh, by the way, could you bring gasoline with you, <name_g>?  I was so angry I forgot to bring it with me…
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  It's such an easy job…
dialogue.advice: Maybe we can find some gasoline at a gas station.
dialogue.success: Sweet, sweet revenge!  Ah, smells so nice!  Feels like the smell of napalm in the morning!  All his stuff, and probably even that <name_b>, will burn to ashes in a matter of minutes.  You helped me get my revenge, so I'll follow you to the end, <name_g>!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: Wow, you failed?  How…

data.description: You could find this place upside down, dizzy and blindfolded.  Its presence is too altered to allow the mercy of ignorance.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: Ah, home sweet home.  It feels like I haven't been here for ages.  Fuck, it looks so horrible now.  I guess it's because of <the_cataclysm>.  Thank you for bringing me here, <name_g>.  Let's eat the cake.

data.dynamic_line: Mmm, delicious.  You know, you are good friend, and a good cook.  I'm glad that I'm with you at the day like this.  Say, what do you think about me going with you?  As you can see, my restaurant is thrashes, my house ruined, the only option left is to travel somewhere, and it's better if I do it with someone.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: I'm just a regular pizzaiolo.  My father was a pizzaiolo, my grandfather was a pizzaiolo and I also became a pizzaiolo.  I was making pizza my whole life, until some American <name_b>s ruined my business!  I couldn't do anything about this, but now, with <the_cataclysm> and <zombies> around, I have a chance to get my revenge!

data.description: Bring the pizzaiolo to <color_light_blue>their rival's house</color> and don't forget to <color_yellow>bring at least 200 units of gasoline</color>.  After you got there, talk to the pizzaiolo to start burning the house.

dialogue.offer: I'm so angry!  I have an enemy that ruined my life, and I want revenge for it!  I don't care about <the_cataclysm>, I just want to burn his <freaking> restaurant!  Will you help me?
dialogue.accepted: Good.  Let's go to his restaurant and fucking burn it!  Oh, by the way, could you bring gasoline with you, <name_g>?  I was so angry I forgot to bring it with me…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.
dialogue.advice: Maybe we can find some gasoline at a gas station.
dialogue.success: Sweet, sweet revenge!  It smells so nice!  His restaurant burns, his legacy is now ruined!  Even if he became a <zombie>, it still good.

data.description: Help pizzaiolo find TrueFoodperson and kick his ass.

dialogue.offer: Ah, it's you, <name_g>.  Wanna continue on my revenge to all American <name_b>s?
dialogue.accepted: Good.  Next stop, Foodplace.  I always hated that place, especially that <freaking> <name_b> in his idiotic mask.  I know he's still alive, hiding in his dumb parody of a restaurant.  Take this bat.  Let's take a visit to him, <name_g>, and kick his <freaking> ass!
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.
dialogue.advice: I heard that these 'restaurants' use some kind of locking system for staff room, so we would need to find a way to get there.
dialogue.success: Another one bite the dust!  We did good, <name_g>.

data.description: Help pizzaiolo take back his restaurant.

dialogue.offer: I need to make a last step to achieve my revenge, and the step is - my pizza parlor.  Before <the_cataclysm>, the bank took my place, and now, some <freaking> <name_b>s occupied it and made it their base!  Just unbelievable, I tell ya.  It's time for me to fight back, deal with this <freaking> <name_b>s and regain my honor.  Are you with me, <name_g>?
dialogue.accepted: Very good.  <lets_go>
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.
dialogue.advice: These <name_b>s might be heavily armed, so we need to prepare to face them.
dialogue.success: Nice, very fucking nice.  Fuck, this placed is thrashed.  <freaking> <name_b>s thrashed my restaurant!  Okay, calm down, calm down, will ya… At least I retrieved my place.  Thank you, <name_g>.  I couldn't make it without you.

dialogue.offer: Now, as my competitors dead, their places are ruined, it's time to relax… I know, let's celebrate it!  Lead me to my house.  Also, we need a cake for that.  What celebration without a cake, right?  I can teach you how to cook it, if you want.
dialogue.accepted: Good.  Bring me chocolate cake and talk to me.
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.
dialogue.advice: If you listened to me very closely, it wouldn't be hard for you to make it.  Good luck, <name_g>.

data.dynamic_line: Sure, I guess.  I don't know if I know anything you don't, you seem like you can handle yourself.  I've made it this far by not engaging whenever possible.  I'm never going to kill all the zombies out there.  Darius and I try not to fight if we can avoid it, and if we can't, we try to always have the advantage.  Numbers, weaponry, terrain.  Zombies are clumsy and stupid so we lead them across bushes and things to trip and stumble.  We take high ground and let them plough into ladders like idiots while we stick 'em with spears from above.  Mostly, though, we try not to be seen.  We use bikes instead of cars because they don't make noise and don't need gas, plus we can take forest trails and things and avoid traffic jams.  Those things are suicide.  We try to avoid the cities, and when we do go close, we stick to the outskirts and raid the outlying houses.  In those, we keep crouched and try to get deep into the building fast, or down into the basement, so that little noises don't carry much and nothing from outside can see us.  Also, zombies being idiots, closing the blinds is a great move.  I always keep a crowbar for opening doors and windows, but I try not to use it if I can avoid it.  Darius can pick locks, which is slower but doesn't make noise.  We get a lot more mileage from raiding gas stations and other rural sites, where if there are a few zombies, we can usually lead them away.

It made eye contact with me and I just started hallucinating shit.  Darius stopped me from falling right off the tower.  Stuff like that is why I think you have to be a bit off your rocker to travel these days unless you have no choice.  Anything we don't know, we turn around and pedal hard. Did part of an electrical engineering degree, then decided it wasn't for me and quit that.  Spent a bit of time doing freelance electrical and programming work, then got recruited by a startup that was designing and programming medical equipment.  I was supposed to be a general technician, but through a weird series of events I wound up in sales, then management.  I hated management, and I'd made a big nest egg from my share stock, so I cashed out and tried to retire young. data.dynamic_line:
You'd be surprised actually!  Metal art has been part of Muslim traditions for years, although that's not why I got into it.  I'm not a very traditional girl.  My parents aren't very traditional either, but my grandparents are really old fashioned and strict.  My sister came out as gay and they made her life really hard; mom and dad thought she should keep it secret, but she didn't believe in that.  I always loved mechanics and working with my hands, so when they started harassing my parents about getting my sister and I married off to nice men so we'd stop being so immoral, I decided to pick a job I liked that would bother them as much as possible.  It was a good choice, not only did it make them livid but I love welding.  I love the feel of standing back and looking at my work, knowing I took a few chunks of scrap metal and made them into something useful.  I love how it feels to make it fit together perfectly.  It just puts me at peace.

I… I do hope my grandparents are okay though.  They were old fashioned, and they made choices I didn't like, but they were family and I still have sweet memories of them from when I was little.  I've had to do a lot more thinking about God since <the_cataclysm>, and while I'd never agree with the decisions they made, I understand more why they thought they had to make them.  They just wanted the whole family to share their relationship with God, in their messed up way.

I was on my way to visit my parents back in Burlington, waiting at a bus station, when the evacuation notices started sounding.  I'd been a little out of touch for a bit and didn't realize how bad the rioting was getting.  When my bus arrived it got repurposed into an evacuation vehicle, and took me here.  I… I didn't used to be very religious, it's just something I was born to, but since this happened I've been thinking a lot more about God, and how grateful I am for His help in surviving.  With things still so difficult, it helps to know He's got some plan for me.

Anyway, mine was the second bus to arrive, and they were just getting some triage and processing stuff set up.  I was put in charge of helping with the wounded, along with Uyen.  Things went a little strange later on… one of the women doing triage and processing had a bit of a hang-up about particular, um, colors of people being allowed into the center.  She claimed to have lost our 'papers', along with a lot of other peoples'.  Thankfully because we'd helped so many we were able to argue that they couldn't leave us out, but there was no space left downstairs by the time we got that sorted, so here we are.

A few people just jumped out and ran for the military for protection.  They… it… it was bad.  The driver managed to get us turned around and booked it, and I guess they didn't chase us. dynamic_line.no: Well, these things are a standard .30 caliber.  They should be compatible with any similar rifle barrel. dynamic_line.yes: They're pretty big.  This isn't something you'd carry around with you. The design should be capable of auto or semi-auto fire, at a range that's pretty comparable to a gunpowder-based weapon.  It takes out some of the most limited parts of ranged weapons: no gunpowder, no brass casings, just lead that we melt into my mold.  It's not soundless, but it's not as loud as a chemical weapon.  There are tons of advantages.  Only trouble is, I can't convince the Free Merchants to give me the parts I need, even though it's for our own defense."  She grimaces. dynamic_line.no: Living here?  Yeah, I guess I live here now.  It's… it's weird.  We're crowded into this tiny space, I don't know these people, but we're sharing bathrooms and we've all been through the same stuff.  It's not great.  At night we can hear the <zombies> outside, and we all just lie there awake, thinking the same things but too scared to talk about it.

yes.no: It's been over a month now, so I guess I'm starting to get used to it.  Things were pretty rough after Sean died, but it wasn't our first big loss and it won't be the last I guess.  I've made a couple friends, and in a weird way we're all like family.  We were all hoping they'd let us downstairs sooner than this though.  We're never quite sure if there's going to be enough food to go around.  I'm really hoping I can lose myself in this project.  Still haven't had a good night's sleep since <the_cataclysm>.

There's good and there's bad.  We're all pretty sick of being cooped up in here for months, never knowing if there's going to be food to eat or not.  It's starting to look like they're never going to let us go down to the secure basement, and none of us have slept well since we were brought in.  We know we've got it pretty good… we're safe, we're alive.  It's just, like, what kind of life are we even living?
yes.yes: It's getting bad.  We've been stuck in here for months, nothing changing, nothing improving.  We can't go outside, we don't have enough to eat, and we didn't choose to be with each other.  I don't know how long we can stay like this before somebody snaps.

data.dynamic_line: They run this place, and they don't run a charity.  We get paid for working around the place, maintaining it, what have you, and we trade cash for food.  The thing is, supply and demand and all… there's a lot more cash than food around.  It's easier to buy a laptop than a piece of beef jerky, and there's no sign of that getting better.  The balance is way off right now, a hard day of work barely gets you enough to fill your belly.  I shouldn't bitch too much though.  I don't know much better way to run it, although rumor is that the folks living downstairs have it a lot easier than we do.  I try not to think too much on that.

Fatima's a sweety, but she's a total dork.  I know, I know, it's backwards for the engineer to call the heavy-duty mechanic a nerd, but hey.  I call it like it is.  She and I have been doing some odd jobs around the upstairs here, fixing up old machinery and things.

Well, Dana lost her baby right after <the_cataclysm>, in a bus rollover.  She was lucky to make it out alive.  She and Pedro had one of the rougher trips here, I guess.  We just kinda click as friends, I'm grateful there's someone else here I can really get along with.  Her husband, Pedro, is still pretty shell-shocked.  He doesn't talk much.  I like him though, when he opens up he's just hilarious.  Draco is just a cantankerous old fart who hasn't actually got old yet, give him twenty years and he'll be there.  I like grumpy people.  We also have pretty similar taste in music.  Aleesha's a sweet kid, and we've all kind of adopted her, but she seems to hang out with me and Dana the most.  She's a great artist, and she's full of crazy ideas.  I guess I like her because of all of us, she seems to have the most hope that there's a future to be had.

dynamic_line.yes: I didn't get to know Boris, Garry, and Stan so well for the first while.  They kinda kept to themselves.  Boris and Stan had just lost their son, you know.  It's pretty lucky that Garry was with them, he's Stan's little brother.  Together, they're a pretty good team.  I feel bad for thinking they were standoffish before.  They probably do the most to pull their weight around here whenever there's work to be done.
dynamic_line.no: Boris and Stan are married, I guess.  They kinda keep to themselves, they seem a bit standoffish if you ask me.  Garry is Stan's brother, I think, but I'm not totally sure.  He seems nice enough, but he's a man of few words.  I can't get a good bead on them.  I've learned not to pry too much though.

dynamic_line.yes: The Singhs are really shy, and I think they feel pretty bad about making it through this together.  They're the only complete family I've seen since <the_cataclysm>.  That has to feel really weird, and I think it's made them stick really close together.  I think… I think they also just don't really like any of us.
dynamic_line.no: I really can't get a bead on them.  They never really talk to anyone outside of their little family group, they just sit in their own spot and speak Punjabi.  They always seem nice, and they do their share, they just don't have any social connection.

dynamic_line.yes: Vanessa… I'm doing my best, I really am, but we just do not get along.  One of these days one of us is probably going to brain the other with a tire iron, and I'm just grateful I spend more time around the tire irons.  Uyen and Rhyzaea are both excellent people, and I genuinely like them, but I can't stand this ongoing political bullshit they've got going on.  Alonso is just a… he's… there's no polite word for what he is.  A lot of the others are fine with it, and okay, sure, I guess.  John is a walking stereotype, but he's a great poker buddy. dynamic_line.no: Vanessa… well, she's nice, I guess.  I gotta say, she kinda drives me nuts, but we're in this together so I try not to be too harsh. "To be honest with you, I made a delivery run here a few months ago to drop off some office supplies.  When I saw the state the world was in, I thought perhaps this would be a safer place to go than many, and so we made our way here.  It was a difficult journey, but I'm sure you've heard many tales of that time, and have your own.  We were nearly gunned down at a road stop, but I knew a back route and managed to slip away.  There was a pickup truck with a travel trailer that tried to take the back route, though, and overturned.  It nearly blocked the road, and the trailer had been full of people.  Many of them were now returned, and were stumbling around.  We made it through, barely, but the car was damaged then.  You get the idea."  He sighs, rubbing his beard idly, his expression flat.  "Somehow, we made it.  What's more, all three of us made it, and again made it through the disaster in the back room here.  We were very lucky.

responses.text: Tell me about yourself.  What did you do before?
Are you kidding?  That sounds like an amazing story.  What happened after you got past the trailer?

data.dynamic_line: *smiles, very briefly, and nods.  "Very well.  The blockage had forced us to go through the woods, and our rusty old sedan was not suited to it.  We must have jarred something loose, because we were not far past the trailer when there was a loud bang, and the wheels stopped turning.  The engine spun and the axles rattled, but it was all sound and fury, signifying nothing.  We'd moved far enough from the overturned trailer to buy time, but as we got out of the vehicle, we could hear their moans on the wind, drawing closer."  As he dives into the story, Mandeep becomes more animated, his resonant accented voice carrying naturally over the rolling cadence of his words.  "I am no mechanic, and even if I were, there was no time for repairs.  We took what we owned and carried on on foot.  The center was not far, I knew, and at least Guneet and I had our kirpan, should we be forced to defend ourselves."  He touches the handle of the sword at his side, giving you a moment to interrupt if you want.

The roads further on were muddy: soon, we couldn't walk any further.  Our pace was enough to keep us ahead of the dead, but I feared for our safety should we stop.  We went on until we had no choice.  Our feet blistered in shoes not meant for such a journey, and our packs weighed us down; we knew that if we met any more zombies, we couldn't escape nor fight them.  At last, a long-abandoned shack gave us refuge, its roof collapsed and its windows boarded up."  He flares his nostrils.  "I had expected some awful smell, and animal dung, but to be honest, it was still surprisingly dry and dusty inside.  We had a packed lunch, and feasted on cold, leftover samosa that night."  With a little wink, he pats his belly.  "I suppose it was the last time I enjoyed my wife's home cooking, in a way.  It was hard to enjoy it.  Under no circumstances could we risk a fire.  We each took a turn guarding in the dark, and got what sleep we could in the cold of that old ruin."  Glancing around at the cramped shelter room, he pauses for a moment.  "It seems almost like a memory that didn't happen, too outlandish to fit with the rest of my mundane life.  The next day dawned, damp and cold, but without pursuers.  By then I was confident we'd lost the zombies."  He gives you a solemn look.  "That is, truly, the end of this story.  Once the sun was up, we made our way through the forest, onto the road, and from there it was a short walk to this center.

I've been to Korea and Slovenia for the same reason.  I guess I'm a bit of a forest tourist?  I don't know if I'll ever see my own forest again, and the thought breaks my heart.

My mom and dad are back in Hazelton, they live with my grandma and my older brother; he took a hard knock to the head doing dumb things as a kid, and he can't really take care of himself now.  I have a daughter, Angel, she's sixteen and didn't want to come with me on this trip.  God help me, I can't bear to think of her, she must think I'm dead.

data.dynamic_line: I'm sorry, but I'm not here to make friends, I've got a job to do.

I'm actually accepting a number of different foodstuffs: beer, sugar, flour, smoked meat, smoked fish, dried fruit and vegetables, cooking oil, preservatives like salt and vinegar; and as mentioned before, jerky, cornmeal, and fruit wine.

We call them "Free Merchant Certified Notes".  We started signing money almost as soon as we got here as a way of showing it represented actual goods and services we had to trade.  Within a few days we'd organized the system, and now it's been evolving into a form of cash.  Internally they're traded for labor and services in exchange for food rations and other trade goods, but we've been using them with suppliers we regularly trade with as well, those that have faith in us.

Yeah, it's a tough situation.  When we started out here nobody was really in charge, and we let more in than we really had capacity to feed and support.  When the dust settled and we'd established a little order, there were still all these people upstairs waiting for a place to live, and no space.  We've set up a little space for them, but it's not ideal.

A couple folks died in there, and it escalated.  One of the first people here, Jacob, had taken charge of the whole thing.  When the triage area had to be evacuated he stayed behind to make sure everyone who could get out got out.  It was a hell of a loss.

data.description: You need to bring me a <color_light_blue>centrifuge</color>, equipment like this can most commonly be found at <color_light_blue>hospitals</color>, but you can also try to search for it at <color_light_blue>medical labs</color> then bring it back to the <color_light_blue>Doctor</color>.

dialogue.describe: It could be very useful to be able to perform an analysis of zombie blood…
dialogue.offer: We don't have the equipment for real analysis here so I'll need you to bring me one.  I've been authorized to reward the completion of this job with 30 merch, a sizeable sum of the local currency.
dialogue.accepted: Excellent.  Here, I'll note the location of a hospital nearby, with some luck you should be able to find a centrifuge in working condition there.
dialogue.rejected: Are you sure?  The data we could extract with that equipment could be priceless…
dialogue.advice: Centrifuges can be a bit heavy; you might want to locate a smaller one if you can, it will be way easier to transport.
dialogue.inquire: Well, do you have the centrifuge yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent!  This may be the key to removing the infection.
dialogue.success_lie: Wait, you couldn't possibly have the centrifuge!  Liar!
dialogue.failure: What a shame, that equipment could have proved invaluable…

dialogue.offer: The medical software didn't just analyze the blood, it triggered a government alert.  Medical staff was under orders to immediately drive any matching samples to the nearest laboratory.  That must mean the government knew!  We have the destination address.  Go there, get in, and bring back any records you can download off a computer.  Like last time, I can compensate you, and the Old Guard saw enough promise in this assignment to spare a larger sum of 60 merch.  I'm sure you're also free to lay claim to any valuables you might find at the target location.
dialogue.accepted: Great!  I've mapped out a route to the address.  Bring back anything you find on this secure USB drive.
dialogue.rejected: Can't blame you, but come back if you change your mind.
dialogue.advice: If the laboratory is locked, maybe you can find an id card from employees who died in the evacuation.  Don't forget the secure USB drive.
dialogue.success: Thanks!  This data looks damaged, but maybe I can make something out of it.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: Unfortunately the data you got was incomplete and mostly encrypted.  There may be a way to get encryption codes, though.  I found a complaint by the infosec team that they were unable to deliver critical security updates to one research site.  It was some kind of more restricted secondary site, they weren't allowed in.  That means it should have unsecured computers we can get the codes from.  I couldn't secure any funding for this due to a lack of obvious results, but if you believe in this enough, maybe we can convince them otherwise?
dialogue.accepted: Great!  I've mapped out a route to the address.  Use this secure USB drive as usual.
dialogue.rejected: Can't blame you, but come back if you change your mind.
dialogue.advice: Expect the lab to be locked as usual.  Don't forget the secure USB drive.
dialogue.success: Wonderful!  Now I just need to get an undamaged, complete archive, and we can really figure out what happened.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: So there looks to be months, maybe years of experiments, and that data set must be huge.  That data will have to be backed up somewhere secure and remote.  I heard of a lab that has data servers hidden in a high security vault on lower floors.  I bet the archives inside that lab are still working.  The Old Guard didn't seem very convinced, but still ended up providing 100 merch for this.
dialogue.accepted: Excellent!  I've mapped out a route to the address.  Bring back anything you find on this secure USB drive.
dialogue.rejected: Can't blame you, but come back if you change your mind.
dialogue.advice: That lab is going to be protected by various security systems.  You may need special access cards or a way to cut your way in.  Don't forget the secure USB drive.
dialogue.success: Thanks!  This is a lot of data to go through.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: In the data we found a major contract for tunneling and train equipment, ordered eight months ago.  It's the best lead we have.  Here's the address of the government lab where the equipment was delivered.  I want you to go there, find the tunnels that they dug, and download everything you can about the train network.  On the other hand, our sponsors were extremely impressed in getting this far without their direction, and would like to apologize by supporting this mission with a whole 300 merch!
dialogue.accepted: So glad for your help.
dialogue.rejected: Can't blame you, but come back if you change your mind.
dialogue.advice: The equipment was rated for 50 feet underground, so that tunnel entrance is going to be deeper inside a lab than a normal subway.  Fifty feet would mean maybe four stories down.  Don't forget the secure USB drive.
dialogue.success: Fantastic!  I should be able to reconstruct what cargo moved between which labs.  I wonder what was really going on down there.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.//: Appears in the refugee center as shopkeeper with missions.  Faction critical.  Real name: Gavin Wheeler

Smokes is a firefighter that volunteered to take stock of what was available and keep inventory. He's gradually had more lumped onto him as the Free Merchants struggle to put themselves together, but he feels obligated to help, even though he doesn't really want to have all the responsibility he does.
data.//2: He's also quite chatty and will gladly talk about the way things are these days. This is deliberate, since Free Merchants are very likely to be the first faction players encounter.
data.//3: Most of his dialogue goes in 'free_merchant_shopkeep_dialogue.json'. Dialogue that just does worldbuilding goes into 'free_merchant_shopkeep_dialogue_fluff.json'.

data.//1: This list tracks the things that Smokes will sell the player.
data.//2: As a general rule of thumb, Smokes should stock tools, spare parts, and other stuff that scavengers bring in; they canonically have a surplus that they trade for food.
data.//3: Speaking of food, Smokes shouldn't ever offer food!  At the moment they need all the stuff they can get.
data.//4: Smokes offers the following things:
data.//5: - A large quantity of merch, always available;
data.//6: - A guaranteed handful of welding gear, like you might find on a garage rack;
data.//7: - Huge quantities of spare parts, such as solder, thread, nails, tailoring supplies, and so on;
data.//9: - Small quantities of low-end melee weapons, with a chance for civilian-grade guns;
data.//10: - A selection of men's and women's clothing;
data.//11: - A lot of assorted tools and other hardware.

data.//: Generic spare parts that can be used in a lot of different places, like nails and such. Thread is included here due to how it's used a lot even outside of tailoring.
data.//2: Also includes duct tape, but it's useful to them too, not just outsiders. They won't sell as much of it as other crafting goods. Same goes for superglue.
data.//3: To a lesser degree, this also includes building materials, but not that many.

data.//: Random tailoring parts, including rags, cloth sheets, and fasteners.
A collection of welding consumables for both steel and aluminum.
Clothes for both men and women. Distribution chance should be even for both sexes.
Ammo for common guns. Note that this is a collection - the shop will always stock some quantity of ammo, even if it doesn't carry guns in a given rotation.
Common weapons. Pistols should be much more common than long weapons, since they're using good weapons for their own defense.
Low-end melee implements. As with guns, they're using good weapons for themselves, so make sure this doesn't have overly strong ones.
Tools you might find in a house or construction site. They have a ton of common stuff to go around, and quite a bit of heavy-duty hardware as well.
data.//2: Groups like home_hw and similar are deliberately excluded here since they spawn things that the merchants would definitely want to hold onto for themselves instead of selling.

data.description: Deliver the FEMA hard drive to the strange group that Smokes mentioned.  Return to the evacuation center when the data's been delivered.

dialogue.success: Oh, good.  I'm glad you're alright; I had no idea what to make of them.  Well, one less thing to worry about.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: At least you came back alive.  Don't sweat it too much - it's no skin off my back.  If they want it that bad, they can come get another copy themselves.

data.description: Clear out the barricaded back area in the refugee center and lay the former leader of the Free Merchants to rest, in exchange for the local currency: Free Merchant certified notes.

assign_mission_target.//: om_special does nothing because we are at the evac_center. I added this to make the linter happy.

dialogue.offer: If you really want to lend a hand we could use your help clearing out the dead in the back bay.  Fearful of going outside during the first days of the Cataclysm we ended up throwing our dead and the zombies we managed to kill in the sealed back bay.  Our promising leader at the time even fell… he turned into something different.  Kill all of them and make sure they won't bother us again.  We can't pay much, besides some of our own internal money which isn't good for that much yet, but it would help us to reclaim the bay.  <color_red>If you accept, I'll tell the guards to immediately take down the barricade in the back.  You should only accept if you're ready to do this now.</color>
dialogue.accepted: Please be careful, we don't need any more deaths.
dialogue.rejected: Come back when you get a chance, we really need to start reclaiming the region.
dialogue.advice: If you can, get a friend or two to help you.
dialogue.inquire: Will they be bothering us any longer?
dialogue.success: Thank you, having that big of a threat close to home was nerve wracking.  Here's some of our local certified notes, we've been paying these to our workers in exchange for supplies.  They're getting some value in the center as a trade item, I'm afraid they're all we have to spare at the moment.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Investigate the last known location of a disappeared scavenger trading party, and eliminate any bandits or raiders in the vicinity in exchange for <reward_count:FMCNote> certified notes.

dialogue.offer: This is a bit more involved than the last request, we recently lost a scavenger party coming to trade with us and would like you to investigate.  We strongly suspect a raider band or horde caught them off-guard.  I can give you the coordinates of their last radio message but little else.  In either case, deal with the threat so that the scavengers can continue to pass through in relative safety.  The best reward I can offer is a claim to the supplies they were carrying, plus thirty certified notes - that's our own internal money, good for trading and such.
dialogue.accepted: Our community survives on trade, we appreciate it.
dialogue.rejected: Come back when you get a chance, we really need to start reclaiming the region.
dialogue.advice: If you can, get a friend or two to help you.
dialogue.success: Thank you, the world is a better place without them.  Two of our more skilled individuals accepted the assistance of the Old Guard in setting up an outpost while you were out.  We didn't have many other options, refugees are still streaming in and we don't know what else to do with our limited food supply.  If you get a chance, you should see if they need your assistance in the future…
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Visit the farming commune and bring the foreman's prospectus back to the refugee center, for <reward_count:FMCNote> certified notes.

dialogue.offer: We recently set out some skilled people to start an outpost, to secure us some food supplies in a safer location.  The new outpost that we've started could use your assistance.  I need you to get the foreman's prospectus before we begin to send additional refugees to the farming commune.  Consult with the foreman to get more detailed tasks.  We've got 50 Certified Notes for you if you can do this for us.
dialogue.accepted: I'm sure the outpost will expand quickly with your assistance.
dialogue.rejected: Come back when you get a chance, we really need to start reclaiming the region.
dialogue.advice: Just follow your map.
dialogue.success: With this we'll be able to convince others to invest in the commune.  Thank you, here's your money.  We also managed to get a manual crank hooked up to the garage in the back, so feel free to make use of that - you've been a great help to us.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Deliver 10 solar panel arrays to help the Free Merchants set up a renewable power grid, in exchange for a handsome reward.

dialogue.offer: We are starting to build new infrastructure here and would like to get a few new electrical systems online… unfortunately our existing system relies on an array of something called RTGs.  Running generators isn't a viable option underground, of course.  We have a big flat roof up top, and if we had a few solar panel arrays we could use them to top up our usage.  We could pay you pretty handsomely to bring us, say, ten solar panel arrays?  If you find any advanced solar panels, those are even better.
dialogue.accepted: If you can do this for us our survival options would vastly increase.
dialogue.rejected: Come back when you get a chance, we really need to start reclaiming the region.
dialogue.advice: Solar panel arrays are pretty common on solar farms and on rooftops.  Each advanced solar panel array is worth two solar panel array.
dialogue.success: Great, I know it isn't much but we hope to continue to expand thanks to your help.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Deliver 100 0.5 L glass jars to the Free Merchants to kickstart their food storage plans.

dialogue.offer: While we've managed to secure day to day food supplies, it's very much hand to mouth.  Our reserves would barely last a few days if something kept our people locked in.  We need a stockpile to avoid that.  Thanks to our outpost we have a bit of meat and vegetables coming in, but we need a better way to preserve them.  Some of our people know enough about food canning that if we had a good stock of canning jars, we could make pickles and canned meats to get us set for the winter.  I'll pay you a premium rate if you can bring us around a hundred jars to get us started.
dialogue.accepted: It'll take a load off my shoulders if I can finally stop worrying about this.
dialogue.rejected: We'll hold for the moment, but I'll get an ulcer if I have to keep worrying.  If you reconsider let me know.
dialogue.advice: Grocery stores, house kitchens, there's plenty of places to look.
dialogue.success: That's one less thing to worry about.  Glad to have someone like you on our side.  Here's 25 merch, and the broker will buy any further glass jars you can find - at a reduced price, we can't keep up the premium rate.  Actually, the broker was saying they had some jobs like this for you, and that it might be easier to just go straight through their office if you want more work.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.dynamic_line: Well, we had an odd group come by maybe two days after the power grid went off.  Two armed guards wearing brown uniforms, and what looked like a government doctor, had a hazmat suit on.  Everyone had masks they never took off.  They looked organized… maybe a military remnant from somewhere close by.

The doctor paid us in advance to get some old FEMA info from our computers here, and told us to deliver the data to an isolated building afterwards.  We still haven't done that.  I'm half worried it might have been some kind of trap, or trick.

responses.text: You seem right to be suspicious.

data.dynamic_line: I could share the dropoff location if you want to bring the drive there for us, but whatever's there, I'm not sure it's worth all the trouble.  I'll reward you for your trouble.

responses.text: That seems fine to me.  I'll take your drive for you.
Actually, I can see why you haven't done it yet.  Hold that thought for now.

data.dynamic_line: I was hoping you'd say that.  It's an old isolated building not too far from here; you should probably just leave the drive to whoever's there and be on your way.  And like I said, be careful approaching the place.  I wouldn't like leading you straight into your death.

responses.text: Don't worry, I'll be careful.  I'll let you know when it's done.

data.dynamic_line: Hmm."  Smokes looks thoughtful, rubbing his chin.  "Well, most of the people downstairs aren't willing to come up for things like that, and a lot of folks that are up here have a lot of bad memories from that.  You could try asking around some of the people we have upstairs, but it'll be tough.  If you have some merch you could spare, though, I could get some people off guard duty and into your little crew for some hazard pay.  You might also have luck asking the Old Guard rep in the southwest bay, near the library - I hear they've got some volunteers lately.

responses.text: [5 merch] Five merch for someone sounds fair to me.
[10 merch] How about ten merch to do it?
Thanks for the advice.  Maybe I'll come back with some more merch.

data.dynamic_line: That's enough to get someone off guard duty, yeah.  Hand it here and I'll set it up."  The money exchanges hands.  "Right.  I haven't updated this list in a while, so some people are still assigned to watch the back bay, which is technically a free shift now.  I'll let one of them know about what's up and they can spend the time helping to clean up back there.  Hope it helps.

Woah, you're really intent, hey?  That's a lot for most people here."  The money exchanges hands.  "That's enough to get two people off guard duty for an afternoon, even with all the ugliness back there.  And you know what?  I'll help out, too, so make that three.  I can appreciate someone who's willing to put their money where their mouth is.
*looks at you cautiously.  "He hasn't been bothering you, has he?  Dave's usually pretty harmless."

responses.text: He wants permission to build himself a little shelter outside of your lobby, somewhere out of the way.  He'd need access to your washrooms and things, but you could clear him out of this space.

data.dynamic_line: Sure, sounds great on paper, but *where*?  We aren't swimming in real estate here, the place is seriously overcrowded.  And I won't have him living out of a soggy cardboard box on the doorstep, it's an even worse look than the lobby.

responses.text: What about the rooftop?  There's a stair access there, I can see it from outside, and he'd probably be able to do a bit of a lookout job.

data.dynamic_line: *rubs his chin.  "It's probably technically a fire hazard, but there's not much to light up there besides what Dave brings.  And a few of the guards are pretty attached to him, so we could maybe send folks up to keep an eye on him and make sure he's doing okay.  That wouldn't interfere with comings and goings, either."  He pauses a moment, looking at his ledger as if it contains answers.  "You know what?  Sure.  If Dave is okay with it, I can talk the others into letting him have rooftop access to build himself a little shelter, as long as he continues to keep it clean up there like he has in here."

responses.text: Thanks.  I'll go let him know.

yes: Welcome back.
Hello again.  What do you need?
*looks up.  "Hey."
dynamic_line.no: *waves you over.  "I haven't seen you before.  Welcome to our little homely house."

responses.text: Who are you?  This is a refugee center, right?
I'm looking for a specific, strange building.  I wonder if you've heard anything about it, maybe from some of the traders coming through?
Just passing through, don't mind me.

dynamic_line: Hope it helps.
Give me second to write that down… okay, done.
You know where to find me.

responses.text: When will you have new stuff in stock?

Other than those people with the hard drive, none that I know of.  Scavengers share some odd things, but we can't exactly go check for ourselves.  The teamster in the back bay might have some pointers, though, if you really want to know.

Things were rough at first, and our policy of taking everyone we could caused a lot of strife later on.  Right now, we just want to get enough trade going keep ourselves afloat.  We might have to turn people away, but we've found that they're usually willing to trade with us, which is our only real source of food right now.  We're trying to turn that into a business model.  Doesn't matter who you are, we'll trade with you as long as you don't bring trouble.

responses.text: What about when the goods dry up?  Won't that happen eventually?

data.dynamic_line: Right now, it's the best way we have to make sure that everyone gets what they need.  Long-term viability of business models is what people in suits used to do back before all this, and we see where that got them.  Barter is the only thing keeping us from starving, so we're going to keep doing it as long as it works or until we can start producing our own food.

I don't think we have a figurehead right now, I think?  If we do, I don't know about it.  For the most part, we all have our own responsibilities and that works to keep us all fed as a group.  I'm the front man for outsiders, the broker keeps tabs on our food, so on and so forth.  We've had some town hall style talks in the cafeteria about setting up a democracy, but there's nothing solid on that right now.

data.dynamic_line: I'm the region's federal liaison.  Most people here call us the 'Old Guard' and I rather like the sound of it.  Despite how things currently appear, the federal government was not entirely destroyed.  After the outbreak I was chosen to coordinate civilian and militia efforts in support of military operations.

responses.text: So what are you actually doing here?

data.dynamic_line: I ensure that the citizens here have what they need to survive and protect themselves from raiders.  Keeping some form of law is going to be the most important element in rebuilding the world.  We do what we can to keep the 'Free Merchants' here prospering and in return they have provided us with spare men and supplies when they can.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: Well… I was like any other civilian till they conscripted me so I'll tell it to you straight.  They're the best hope we got right now.  They are stretched impossibly thin but are willing to do what is needed to maintain order.  They don't care much about looters since they understand most everyone is dead, but if you have something they need… you WILL give it to them.  Since most survivors here have nothing they want, they are welcomed as champions.

data.dynamic_line: There isn't much pushed out by public relations that I'd actually believe.  From what I gather, communication between the regional force commands is almost non-existent.  What I do know is that the 'Old Guard' is currently based out of the 2nd Fleet and patrols the Atlantic coast trying to provide support to the remaining footholds.

I don't know much about how it formed but it is the armada of military and commercial ships that's floating off the coast.  They have everything from supertankers and carriers to fishing trawlers… even a few NATO ships.  Most civilians are offered a cabin on one of the liners to retire to if they serve as a federal employee for a few years.

They may just be propaganda but apparently one or two cities were successful in 'walling themselves off.'  Around here I was told that there were a few places like this one but I couldn't tell you where.

You can't actually join unless you go through a recruiter.  We can usually use help though, ask me from time to time if there is any work available.  Completing missions as a contractor is a great way to make a name for yourself among the most powerful men left in the world.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: If you want to know what our next steps are, I'm not at liberty to tell you.  Truth be told, I don't even know myself.  They don't share that sort of information with me.

data.description: Go to the supposed source of the weird robots marked on your map and report back to the Old Guard representative what you've seen.

dialogue.offer: I don't usually hear much from command, but we got a message by radio recently.  You might be the right choice to look into it for me.  There've been reports of weird robots and things wandering around since things went south.  Dunno how, but apparently command tracked down what they think is the source.  They want someone to go check out who is making these, and if we can get any tech or assistance from them. dialogue.accepted: Thanks, keeping the people safe is what we try and do.
dialogue.rejected: Come back when you get a chance, we really need to start reclaiming the region.
